emission.protocol-compiler: wherever no source-replacement certificate is demanded (untrusted-source mode, or d_A = 1) and the letter alphabet X has at least two letters; at one letter {M_x} is the identity on A and ass:alice-meas holds of every device

A-ALICE-MEAS.summary: Where no source-replacement certificate is demanded, in untrusted-source mode or at d_A = 1, and at least two letters are declared, Alice's letter in every round is the outcome of her declared measurement on that round's system A alone, whatever happens in the other rounds.
A-ALICE-MEAS.title: Alice's declared measurement where no source certificate is demanded
A-ALICE-MEAS.user_statement: Applies where no source-replacement certificate is demanded and at least two letters are declared. Where the system A is one-dimensional, the declared measurement is only the probabilities of Alice's letter, which is then her local randomness; with a trusted source the engine refuses letter probabilities that differ from the source's and a sent state that depends on the letter. With an untrusted source and A of dimension two or more, Alice measures at her station the system A she receives. In every round she obtains her letter by the same declared measurement on that round's system alone, whatever happens in other rounds, their outcomes and the public messages included. Systems from an untrusted source, being the adversary's, may be correlated across rounds. A device of Alice's declared as a measured factor is a receiver measurement of the specification, not covered here.
A-ALICE-MEAS.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.statistics: on every result, the constructed box and a declared singleton alike

A-ALPHABET.summary: In every one of the n rounds of the run an acceptance value of the alphabet is recorded. The counts and the frequency vector then describe the whole run, normalised by its round count.
A-ALPHABET.title: An acceptance value recorded in every round
A-ALPHABET.user_statement: Every one of the n rounds of your run records an acceptance value from the declared acceptance alphabet: no round counted in n is missing from the record. If rounds go missing (for example through lost time tags), the counts are normalised against the wrong number of rounds and the acceptance test does not describe the run. A round missing from the record also puts security at stake: the acceptance test must be evaluated on the acceptance values of all n rounds ([[A-CONFORM]]), and a measured round the record drops is a sifting step the declaration does not describe ([[A-SPEC]]). Where the engine builds the acceptance set, it checks that the alphabet, its order and n are those of your protocol declaration; a set carried in the declaration is read in the declaration's order, so writing it in that order is yours to check.
A-ALPHABET.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.meat-core: whenever the constraint list is non-empty and a key length is wanted, on a run that reports a key length or a first-order bound
emission.protocol-compiler: whenever m >= 1 and a key-length-eligible declaration is wanted

A-ATK.summary: For a licensed non-empty constraint list that backs a key-length claim, its producer's reduction represents every physical attack with finite registers and every signal at its first channel by an admissible attack sequence. It lets constraints restrict the attacks considered.
A-ATK.title: Attack-set licence
A-ATK.user_statement: Applies only where constraints restrict the attacks the analysis considers, each in the form your declared source mode admits, which the engine checks. Whoever produced the reduction chain has proved that every attack on your physical system becomes, after the reduction, an attack that respects every listed constraint in every round. The proof is asked of attacks with a finite-dimensional memory, of any size, that receive every signal at the start; the engine extends the security statement to every other attack by a limit ([[meat-core/cor:composed-security]]). For constraints the reductions module produces and certifies, that proof is its licence theorem. A constraint you add yourself, or one supplied without such a certificate, needs that proof from you, or must be removed; the analysis without constraints stays valid.
A-ATK.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.meat-core: on every run that reports a key length, with the declared eps_auth and k_auth bound to it, zeros included

A-AUTH.summary: Every classical message travels through an authentication scheme using at most k_auth bits of pre-shared key and realising the authenticated classical channel within ε_auth, a reused key's distance from an ideal one included. It is the premise by which authentication enters the key's security.
A-AUTH.title: Authentication of the classical channel by a keyed scheme
A-AUTH.user_statement: Every classical message of your protocol, per-round announcements included, is protected by one authentication scheme: the attacker may read, delay or block any message, but one she alters or injects, or delivers before it was sent, is rejected except within an error ε_auth. It uses at most k_auth bits of pre-shared secret key per run. That error is its composable error on two identical copies of a uniform, independent key plus the distance of the parties' actual copies from such a pair (zero for a fresh key; for a key from an earlier run, a distance you must bound, which that run's security parameter alone does not bound); declare that sum as ε_auth and the bits used as k_auth. No composable proof for this timing-aware channel is published yet; Wegman–Carter authentication with separate keys per direction approximates it. Both declared zero assert a keyless authenticated channel.
A-AUTH.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.protocol-compiler: whenever a public choice of either form is declared anywhere in the specification: a choice-weighted presentation of Alice's measurement, a choice-weighted physical family of any measured factor, or a `choice_weighting` of any measured factor, whichever party's

A-COIN.summary: Every public choice is drawn with its declared bias; those of fixed bias are jointly independent of each other, the quantum systems and the adversary, and one weighted by a station's setting depends on the round through that setting only. It lets a weight inside the measurement describe the round.
A-COIN.title: Public choices as private coins of declared bias
A-COIN.user_statement: Every public choice of your protocol (for example an actively chosen basis, or whether a round is a test round; a basis set passively by a beam splitter is part of the measurement, not a choice), whichever party draws it and at whichever of its stations, comes from a local random number generator with exactly the declared probabilities, and each is announced or kept secret exactly as declared. The choices with fixed probabilities are independent of each other and, all together, of the quantum signals and of anything an attacker does. A choice whose probabilities depend on a station's private setting is drawn by a party whose recorded outcome includes that setting, and may depend on that setting only, never otherwise on Alice's letter, another choice or a detection result.
A-COIN.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.meat-core: on every run that reports a key length

A-CONFORM.summary: The implementation applies the acceptance test and the verification abort, sends no message beyond the model's, outputs the model's key or nothing, uses no key before the execution ends and aborts on an authentication failure. It ties the analysed protocol to the one that runs.
A-CONFORM.title: The implementation runs the analysed post-processing
A-CONFORM.user_statement: Your implementation runs exactly the analysed post-processing. It aborts unless the acceptance statistics lie in the declared acceptance set; after the rounds it sends no public message other than the error-correction transcript of at most λ_EC bits and its seed, the verification seed, hash and result, the privacy-amplification hash choice and the closing accept or abort decisions; it aborts when verification fails or a message fails authentication (an auth-abort); it outputs the analysed ℓ-bit key, or nothing. No part of the key is used before the execution has ended: the key holder, having sent its final decision, waits until the partner has received it or an auth-abort in its place, and the partner until one of these has arrived. Interactive error correction, a resent syndrome or early key use violate this. Tightening 2ε_auth to ε_auth under this timing is an open question.
A-CONFORM.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.reductions: only where the emitted constraint list is non-empty, a condition on the constants of emitted entries holding vacuously of an empty list (ass:constdecl; req:assumption-ledger)

A-CONST.summary: Every constant of an emitted constraint entry is fixed before the run by the device fact that certifies it and is no function of an observed statistic. Observed data reach the analysis only through the acceptance set, which belongs to another module.
A-CONST.title: Declared constants of the constraint list
A-CONST.user_statement: Applies only where the reduction emits constraints on the attacker; a run that emits none does not rest on it. Every number used as a constant in such a constraint (for example a bound on a detector's multi-photon response) is fixed before the run from the device characterisation that justifies it. It is never adjusted using data observed in the run; observed data enter only through the acceptance test.
A-CONST.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

A-EIG.summary: Where an exact window is evaluated in floating point, the declared slack bounds any overestimate of the exact block minimum eigenvalue by the computed one. This one-sided premise on the arithmetic is the price of that window; a setting without one, or evaluated rigorously, does not invoke it.
A-EIG.title: Declared slack on the computed block eigenvalues
A-EIG.user_statement: Applies only if you request an exact-window depth at a setting whose weight the receiver evaluates in floating point. Wherever your declaration describes a valid receiver exactly, the receiver evaluates the weight rigorously instead, from a proved lower bound on each block eigenvalue, and does not use this premise; the record says which evaluation each setting got. Where it falls back to floating point, the eigensolver that computes the smallest eigenvalue of each requested high-photon block may overestimate it by at most the slack ε_eig you declared. The engine cannot check this and trusts its floating-point eigensolver up to ε_eig. Without an exact-window request this premise is not used, and the bound comes from a closed form that rests on no premise about the eigensolver.
A-EIG.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.protocol-compiler: read off the transmitter artefact's own ledger

A-ENS.summary: The physical source draws each round's letter independently with the declared weights and emits the product of the declared states, no round depending on another. It ties a source specification declared as matrices to the device it describes.
A-ENS.title: Emission of the specified ensemble
A-ENS.user_statement: Your source prepares, in every round, one of the declared states with the declared probabilities. Each round's letter is drawn independently with weights p_x, and the states emitted over the n rounds form a product: no round's letter or state depends on another round, its detection results or its public messages. A source with memory or drift between rounds (for example pattern effects in a modulator) violates this. Where your source is a pair source inside your laboratory with one half measured there to herald or fix the letter, those local detectors belong to the declared ensemble: their efficiency mismatch must be carried by the declared weights and states, and their memory across rounds (for example afterpulsing or dead time) violates this like any other dependence between rounds.
A-ENS.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

A-EVE-DIM.summary: Every register of the adversary, her initial register and her memories, is finite-dimensional, with no bound on its dimension. No claim rests on it: the analysed models have such registers by definition, and [[meat-core/cor:composed-security]] reaches an adversary whose memory has any dimension.
A-EVE-DIM.title: The adversary's registers are finite-dimensional
A-EVE-DIM.user_statement: No run rests on this assumption: the security statement of a run holds against an attacker whose quantum memory has any size, finite or infinite ([[meat-core/cor:composed-security]]). The assumption states that the attacker's quantum memory is finite-dimensional, of any size she likes.
A-EVE-DIM.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

A-EXACT.summary: Declared component parameters, efficiencies, dark-count probabilities and probe mean photon numbers are exact. A non-zero parameter tolerance would be an uncertainty set, which is out of scope and is refused rather than ignored.
A-EXACT.title: Exact declared parameters
A-EXACT.user_statement: Every number you declared for a receiver component (each efficiency, dark-count probability, probe mean photon number and other component parameter) is the device's true value, not an estimate with an error bar. The engine refuses a non-zero tolerance field, and an uncertainty set is not modelled. A result computed from a measured value therefore applies to a device with exactly that value.
A-EXACT.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.meat-core: on every run that reports a key length

A-FIXED.summary: The acceptance set, the round count, the key length, the transcript length, the error budgets, the authentication parameters and the Rényi order are fixed before the run and applied unchanged. The key length is that of a fixed-length protocol, not one chosen from the run's data.
A-FIXED.title: Protocol parameters fixed before the run
A-FIXED.user_statement: Every parameter the key length rests on is fixed before the run starts: the acceptance test, the number of rounds, the key length, the error-correction budget λ_EC, the error budgets ε_PA and ε_EV, and the authentication parameters ε_auth and k_auth. The Rényi order α at which the key length is computed is fixed before the run too; choosing it by comparing the key lengths your declared model gives at several orders, as the run tier's outer search over α does, reads no data of the run and is such a choice. None of them may be chosen or adjusted after looking at the run's data, for example by relaxing the acceptance threshold or picking the key length from the observed error rate. That would be a variable-length protocol, which this analysis does not cover.
A-FIXED.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.meat-core: on every run that reports a key length

A-HASH.summary: Privacy amplification uses an ideal two-universal family, collision probability exactly 2^−ℓ for distinct inputs, and error verification a two-universal family. The first is what leftover hashing reads, the second what the verification collision bound reads.
A-HASH.title: Ideal two-universal privacy amplification
A-HASH.user_statement: Privacy amplification uses a hash family in which any two different inputs collide with probability exactly 2^−ℓ (an ideal two-universal family, such as Toeplitz hashing), and error verification uses a two-universal hash family. If your privacy-amplification family is only two-universal (collision probability at most 2^−ℓ), shorten the key by one further bit.
A-HASH.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.statistics: on a declared singleton only, whose completeness figure (singleton/thm:singleton-completeness) rests on it; the construction map never emits one, and the singleton's honest input is a single law

A-HON.summary: On an honest run the acceptance statistics are independent and identically distributed with the declared law. The premise bears on the advertised honest abort probability and restricts no adversary.
A-HON.title: Honest i.i.d. rounds
A-HON.user_statement: Without an eavesdropper, every round's acceptance outcome is drawn independently from the same declared distribution. If you expect drift between or within runs, declare an honest envelope instead. This premise only bears on the advertised probability that an honest run aborts: if it fails, an honest run may abort more or less often than advertised. Security is unaffected.
A-HON.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.statistics: on every result of the construction map, the canonical box it emits: its completeness figure (binomial-box/thm:completeness-bound) rests on it, a single law being the degenerate envelope (lem:hon-degenerate)

A-HON-ENV.summary: On an honest run each round's probability of each acceptance outcome, given everything before it, stays inside the declared honest envelope. The premise bears on the advertised honest abort probability and restricts no adversary.
A-HON-ENV.title: Honest rounds inside a declared envelope
A-HON-ENV.user_statement: When no attacker is present, each round's probability of each acceptance outcome, given everything that happened before, stays inside the honest model: between the lower and upper bounds of the honest envelope where you declared one, and equal to the honest distribution where you gave a single one instead (an envelope of zero width). With an envelope the channel may drift within and between runs as long as it stays inside it; with a single distribution it may not drift at all. This premise only bears on the advertised probability that an honest run aborts; it never affects security. If drift can leave the honest model, declare a wider envelope.
A-HON-ENV.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

A-IDEAL.summary: On the Band-A route the declared receiver is an exactly projective qubit measurement with unit efficiency and no loss, dark counts, multi-photon events or misalignment, on a transmitted system that is exactly a qubit. The route is an explicit idealization, not a squashing argument.
A-IDEAL.title: Ideal qubit receiver on the Band-A route
A-IDEAL.user_statement: Only for an idealised Band-A analysis: your receiver is a perfect qubit measurement, with unit detection efficiency, no loss, no dark counts, no multi-photon events and no misalignment, and what reaches it in each round is exactly one qubit. The engine refuses a Band-A declaration whose own numbers contradict this: more than one measuring station, a measured system (or, with a trusted source, a transmitted system) of dimension other than two, or a measurement not made of projectors (per basis, where a basis choice is declared). No real optical receiver meets this; use the route to reproduce textbook comparison values. Declare a real device through the receiver module and a squashing reduction.
A-IDEAL.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.meat-core: on every run that reports a key length

A-KEYREG.summary: The post-processing acts on the raw-key string the rounds write, the declared holder computes that string, and reconciliation runs one way from the holder through a padded fixed-length transcript. The leakage term counts the register's full length.
A-KEYREG.title: Dedicated key register and one-way reconciliation
A-KEYREG.user_statement: Error correction is one-way. The key holder computes its raw key from its own record (its letters, the detection results of its measuring stations, or both, whichever it holds) and the public announcements, and its messages depend only on that raw key and public random seeds. The transcript always has exactly λ_EC bits, shorter messages being padded. Interactive error correction (for example Cascade) or a variable-length transcript is not covered by this key length.
A-KEYREG.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.meat-core: once per party of the declaration, its row naming the party: on a run that reports a key length, at both parties, unconditionally, as thm:keylength assumes it at each of the two; on a run that reports a first-order bound and no key length, in trusted-source mode only and only at the party to which the party partition assigns A, the one instance thm:accumulated-entropy uses, and in untrusted-source mode not at all

A-LAB.summary: Nothing about a party's records leaves its laboratory but its key, the public messages and, in trusted-source mode at the party of A, the emitted systems; the adversary acts on it only through what its declared measurements receive and the messages. It excludes side channels at both parties.
A-LAB.title: Each party's laboratory is sealed
A-LAB.user_statement: Whatever a party's role, nothing about its letters, settings, choices, detection results, keys or random numbers leaves its laboratory but the final key, the public messages and, where the party sends with a trusted source, the signals that source emits; timing and auxiliary signals reveal no more. An untrusted source counts as outside every laboratory, even one it is in. The attacker reaches a laboratory only via the systems its declared measurements receive and the public messages. Light sent in to read out a letter, a setting, a choice or a detector state (a Trojan-horse attack, at a receiver as at a modulator), emanations from any device, detector back-flash and anything but the declared input modes influencing a measurement violate this, a clock or trigger line from an untrusted source included; where it sends with a trusted source, so does light seeding or recalibrating its laser.
A-LAB.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.protocol-compiler: everywhere but Band A, where the one link is decided to be the identity, supplied as data, with the identity outcome correspondence and, by (C4), the declared family as its target POVM (req:band-a-identity-link), and thm:band-a (v) proves every clause of it, and but a specification with an empty source segment each of whose measured factors has as its receiver segment the single instance link of a reductions artefact of this run, exact, with no channel supplied as data and the identity outcome correspondence, where reductions/thm:emit (iii), thm:chain (i)-(iii) and thm:transfer prove every clause factor by factor and reductions/thm:emitted-product (ii), (iii) with thm:licence (v) jointly, the apparatus measuring the product of the factors' families by A-MEAS (reductions/ass:meas) (iv) (rem:obligations-discharged; req:link-row-provenance)

A-LINK.summary: Every link of the reduction chain is sound: its channel exists and is a channel, the reduced protocol's security implies the physical one's, and every transported constraint holds on reachable states. A decided pullback or source identity is a necessary condition only, never this obligation.
A-LINK.title: Soundness of every reduction link
A-LINK.user_statement: Every reduction step between your physical devices and the finite model the engine solves is sound, and so is their combination. Each step's channel exists, a channel supplied as numbers is a genuine quantum channel, and a receiver step maps the model's measurement back to the physical one. Security of the reduced protocol implies security of the physical one, and every constraint a step passes on holds for every state an attacker can reach. The run lists this premise wherever it cannot point to a proof: it is not listed on the idealised Band-A route, whose one step is checked to be the identity, nor where every measuring device's single reduction step was built in this run by the engine's reductions module with status exact, with no source step and outcomes kept as they are, where that module's theorems prove it. A chain or channel from elsewhere must come with the proof.
A-LINK.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.meat-core/frank-wolfe: on no run: superseded, and in the closure of no live claim

A-LMO.summary: At every iterate a first-order bound uses, the block list consumed from the oracle, any positivity repair included, puts the linear form of the gradient its bracket consumes at or below its minimum over the exact Choi feasible set. No claim rests on it: [[meat-core/frank-wolfe/lem:feasible-side-dual]] bounds that minimum instead.
A-LMO.title: Exact linear minimisation over the feasible set
A-LMO.user_statement: No run rests on this assumption: the engine verifies a lower bound on the solver's linear minimisation in exact arithmetic instead of trusting it. The assumption states that at every step whose bound the engine uses, the semidefinite-programming solver returned a block list at which the linear objective it was asked to minimise, the gradient of the objective the bound is taken for, is no larger than its true minimum over the exact feasible set, after the engine's small positivity repair of the return.
A-LMO.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.reductions: on every emission, at each station. Clause (iv) is a condition on the product of the measurements at the declaration's measured factors, whichever parties carry their labels, and across the parties' parts of def:protocol; the row of each station asserts that same clause, which is vacuous at one measured factor and one measuring party, so it is read once for the run and needs no emission of its own

A-MEAS.summary: In every round each measuring party's device acts as one POVM: it emits a classical outcome, retains no quantum system, and everything after it acts on classical data. It is the hypothesis about the devices behind the output-state equality of the physical and the squashed protocol.
A-MEAS.title: Each measuring party's device as one POVM per round
A-MEAS.user_statement: Each measuring device, at every measuring station of either party, turns the incoming quantum signal into a classical result in every round and keeps nothing quantum afterwards: no post-measurement system is stored, re-used or passed on. Everything after detection (announcements, sifting, acceptance, the key map, error correction, privacy amplification) uses classical data only. Where several measuring stations are declared, of different parties or of one, or where several parties measure inside one declared station, each device measures independently of the others, so that the round's measurement is the product of theirs: no shared randomness or shared ancilla couples them. A receiver with a quantum memory that keeps the measured light, or passes it on, violates this.
A-MEAS.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

A-MODES.summary: Every optical path from outside the receiver to a detector is a declared mode. A bright-illumination or wavelength-shifted attack targets exactly this premise.
A-MODES.title: Completeness of the declared modes
A-MODES.user_statement: Every way light from outside can reach one of your detectors (every spatial, spectral, temporal and polarisation mode it can arrive in) is represented by one of the declared modes. Light the model does not carry, for example at another wavelength or along a path straight to the detectors as in bright-illumination attacks, violates this. Declare the mode, or declare a model of the attack. This premise is about the completeness of the receiver's optical description; that nothing reaches the station except through its declared inputs, and that nothing leaks out of it, is the laboratory premise of this station's party, [[A-LAB]].
A-MODES.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

A-NOSEL.summary: The receiver configuration and the probe declaration are fixed before the run and cannot be chosen or influenced by the adversary. With [[A-TRUST]] this makes one declared POVM, rather than a family, the right object.
A-NOSEL.title: Device fixed independently of the adversary
A-NOSEL.user_statement: Your receiver's configuration (its components and their settings, which output goes to which detector, and the probe settings) is fixed before the run. An attacker cannot choose or change it, including through properties the model does not describe, such as the wavelength of injected light shifting a beam splitter's ratio. If an attacker can steer the receiver this way, the declared measurement is the wrong one and the result does not apply. This premise is about the configuration of the receiver itself; what may leave or enter the station by other routes is the laboratory premise of this station's party, [[A-LAB]].
A-NOSEL.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

A-PASSIVE.summary: Every optical element is passive linear optics, with no gain and no mixing of creation and annihilation operators. Total photon number is then a conserved grading, on which every block statement of the module rests.
A-PASSIVE.title: Passive linear optics
A-PASSIVE.user_statement: Every optical component of your receiver is passive and linear: beam splitters, wave plates, polarisers, attenuators and the like. No component amplifies light, and none is nonlinear (no frequency conversion, no squeezing). The total photon number is then never increased inside the receiver. If a component can add photons, the photon-number blocks the analysis rests on do not exist.
A-PASSIVE.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

A-PORT.summary: A port clicks exactly when the modes it collects carry at least one photon, whatever their distribution over those modes. It is the multimode form of [[A-THRESH]], and it gives a detector that collects several modes a meaning.
A-PORT.title: Mode-insensitive port response
A-PORT.user_statement: Each detector port clicks exactly when at least one photon arrives in any of the modes it collects, whatever their distribution over those modes. A detector whose click probability depends on the spatial, spectral or temporal mode of the arriving photon (efficiency mismatch) violates this. Such a mismatch has to be declared as mode-dependent loss in front of the port.
A-PORT.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.reductions: at a station only where its declared setting set T has at least two values: at T = {*}, q_* = 1, every clause of ass:probe holds of the one setting drawn with weight one (req:assumption-ledger)

A-PROBE.summary: A station's private per-round setting is drawn from its party's own randomness with the declared class weights, independently of the adversary and the round's quantum input, never inferred from an outcome. It lets the setting enter a joint outcome under one common squashing channel.
A-PROBE.title: The station's private setting drawn from its own declared randomness
A-PROBE.user_statement: The station's private setting in each round (for the optical instance, how its probe is switched) is chosen by a random number generator of the station's own party with exactly the declared probabilities. It is independent of anything the attacker does and of the light arriving in that round, and it is never derived from a detection result. An attacker who can predict or influence the setting violates this.
A-PROBE.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.statistics: on every result of the construction map, the canonical box it emits: the box's honest containment (binomial-box/thm:honest-containment) rests on it

A-REACH.summary: Some feasible state of the consuming declaration produces a law of the declared honest envelope, for a single declared law that law itself. It rules out an incompatibility of the honest model with the declaration.
A-REACH.title: An honest law produced by a feasible state
A-REACH.user_statement: Your honest model fits your protocol declaration: a state the declaration admits as feasible produces acceptance statistics in your declared honest envelope, or equal to your single declared honest law. If it fails, the declared devices do not describe the statistics and a key length for them is not warranted. The engine's own honest models are built to match the declared Alice marginal; nothing proves this premise for them. Unless switched off, the engine checks every run whose honest statistics you supply or whose declaration carries a constraint you declared: from a proven mismatch it states a cap on the probability that devices behaving as the declaration says pass your acceptance test, and refuses the run where that cap is at most one half, a threshold you can set. On an unchecked run a mismatch goes undetected and this premise is yours to vouch for.
A-REACH.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

A-RECV.summary: A supplier artefact read by a reduction instance is that module's own output at the accepted version it declares, and the device facts its claims state hold of the numbers exactly as declared. It is the premise behind a reduction on supplier numbers, save an exact, rigorous artefact the run built.
A-RECV.title: Supplier artefact whose claims hold of the device
A-RECV.user_statement: The receiver data your reduction uses (blocks, high-photon weights with their quantifier domain, dark-count channel) come from a receiver artefact produced by an accepted version of the receiver module, the version the artefact names, on the inputs it names, with its own validation results attached, and the device facts that module's claims state are true of those numbers exactly as declared, under its own assumptions. Where this run built it from a declaration describing a valid receiver exactly, every weight evaluated rigorously, both halves follow and the report omits this premise ([[reductions/req:recv-row-provenance]]). For another artefact this run built, acceptance is the status the report gives the receiver's claims and you rely on the second half, floating-point weights included; a receiver file from outside the run needs your own justification for both halves.
A-RECV.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.meat-core: on every run that reports a key length or a first-order bound (the compiler emits it always)

A-RHOM.summary: The same specification, source mode and operators describe every round: the sameness clause of round homogeneity, not the absence of memory across rounds. One compiled declaration and one certificate decision then serve the whole run.
A-RHOM.title: Round homogeneity of the declaration
A-RHOM.user_statement: One protocol description covers the whole run. Every round uses the same measurements, the same setting choices and their probabilities, and the same classical processing, and, where the source is trusted, the same source, so one declaration and one certificate decision apply to all n rounds. A run in which you change settings, or your devices drift so that later rounds need different operators, violates this. Only parts of a run fixed before it starts, each processed as its own execution and composed under [[A-SEPARATE]], which also asks that no device carry a state from one part into the next, can be analysed separately; a split chosen after seeing the data is not covered. That no device remembers earlier rounds is not part of this premise: for the measuring stations it is [[A-SPEC]], for Alice's letter [[A-ALICE-MEAS]], and where the source is trusted the source premise.
A-RHOM.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

A-ROUND.summary: The same instrument, probe declaration and dark-count channel describe every round, and the receiver has no memory across rounds. One receiver artifact then describes the whole run.
A-ROUND.title: Round homogeneity of the instrument, probe and dark counts
A-ROUND.user_statement: Your receiver behaves the same way in every round: the same optics, the same probe settings and the same dark-count behaviour. Nothing it does in one round depends on the inputs or outputs of other rounds: no detector memory, and no drift that the declaration averages over. A receiver whose efficiency drifts during the run violates this. Only parts of a run fixed before it starts, each processed as its own execution and composed under [[A-SEPARATE]], can be analysed separately; a split chosen after seeing the data is not covered. A receiver whose detectors remember earlier clicks, through afterpulsing, a dead time or any other dependence on earlier rounds, violates it too, and nothing in this engine repairs that: no input describes more than one round.
A-ROUND.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

A-ROUND-SQ.summary: One physical POVM describes the measurement of every round, and each round's measurement acts as it describes whatever happened in other rounds: no detector memory and no drift. Nothing is assumed about the attacks being independent across rounds.
A-ROUND-SQ.title: Round homogeneity of the physical measurement
A-ROUND-SQ.user_statement: Each measuring device, at every measuring station of either party, performs the same measurement in every round: the same optics, detectors and dark-count behaviour, settings drawn with the same probabilities, and, where you declared detector-response modes, the same response in each mode. What a device does in one round does not depend on the inputs or outputs of other rounds. Drift of efficiency, alignment or dark counts violates this. Only parts of a run fixed before it starts, each processed as its own execution and composed under [[A-SEPARATE]], can be analysed separately; a split chosen after seeing the data is not covered. Detector memory (afterpulsing, a dead time, any dependence on earlier rounds) violates it too, and nothing here repairs that. Attacks may still correlate the rounds. The engine's finite model and squashing map are its own construction, not part of this premise.
A-ROUND-SQ.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

A-SEED.summary: The post-processing seeds are drawn with their declared laws, privately, independently and afresh; in trusted-source mode the source's letters and prepared systems are independent of the adversary, who never gets a purification of them. Leftover hashing and source replacement rest on it.
A-SEED.title: Private, independent and fresh local randomness
A-SEED.user_statement: Your random choices come from a good private random number generator. The error-correction seed, the error-verification hash and the privacy-amplification hash are each drawn with their intended distribution, kept secret until the protocol announces them, independent of each other, of every other record of the protocol (the raw key included) and of everything the attacker knows, and drawn anew in every run. With a trusted source, the randomness with which it picks each round's letter and prepares its state is uncorrelated with the attacker at the start, and no purification of a prepared state is ever available to the attacker. A seed reused across runs, fixed in the device or disclosed early, or a predictable or pre-shared random source, violates this.
A-SEED.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

A-SEPARATE.summary: Several executions, fixed in advance and run against one adversary, touch none of each other's registers, leave their keys unused until all have ended, and keep their own premises with the others counted as the adversary's. It is what lets their security parameters add.
A-SEPARATE.title: Executions that share no key and no device state
A-SEPARATE.user_statement: You run several executions, one after another or at the same time, and want their security parameters to add. Their number and parameters are fixed before the first starts. Each execution has its own key material, randomness, seeds and pre-shared authentication key, such as a separate part of one pool. No device, memory or random source carries information between them. An execution has ended once both parties have fixed their output, key or abort, after the closing messages; no key is used or read, and nothing else leaks from an ended one, until all have ended. The assumptions each execution's run record lists must still hold when an attacker holds and runs every other execution, her memory, which then holds their systems, of any dimension. A key that authenticates another execution, a key used early, or parameters chosen from an earlier execution's data violate this.
A-SEPARATE.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.meat-core: on every run that reports a key length or a first-order bound (the transmitter emits it always)
emission.protocol-compiler: read off the transmitter artefact's own ledger

A-SEQ.summary: Each round runs the delivery of its quantum systems, then every party's measurement, then the round's public messages, then sifting; each party measures in round order, post-processing follows all rounds and every message is public. It is the timing premise of the security analysis.
A-SEQ.title: Sequential round structure
A-SEQ.user_statement: In every round the quantum systems come first: where your source is trusted, it prepares and sends that round's signal, and otherwise the systems of the round are delivered to the measuring stations. Then every party that measures completes its measurement, and only then are that round's public messages sent, in the declared order. Sifting is then determined by the announcements, and no operation on a quantum system of a round depends on a public message of that round. All classical post-processing (for example error correction, verification and privacy amplification) runs after all n rounds, and every classical message is public. A message sent before a measurement of the same round has finished (for example an early basis announcement) violates this. Each party that measures completes its measurement of each round before it completes that of the next round.
A-SEQ.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.reductions: whenever the run's record names a moved class of the normalizer or a moved block of the declaring party's snap as resting on it (thm:emit (vi); foundations/req:snap-reference (iii)), and never for a kept one or one evaluated off its snap (foundations/def:evaluated-off-snap): in a run whose key length is formed from a number on the reference companion (req:reference-companion; meat-core/frank-wolfe/req:bracket-on-reference), no class of the normalizer and no handed block of the instance snap rests on it, and only the moved blocks on which the companion carries the snapped block can (cor:reference-companion (v)); where it is formed instead on the searched declaration, after a withdrawn bracket (its causes, factor_enclosure_inconsistent among them, meat-core/frank-wolfe/req:bracket-on-reference (iv)) or in the certified evaluation's fallback (cause companion_not_certified, meat-core/frank-wolfe/req:certified-evaluation (i)), they rest on it. A block whose data the declaring party computes from a model not exact on it is moved even where the snap leaves that evaluation unchanged (foundations/def:snap). Each resting block or class carries its group: no usable reference, reference bracket withdrawn, reference bracket not evaluated, or last resort. A run whose every block and class is kept, as at a shipped default whose blocks are all exact on the lattice, does not engage it

A-SNAP.summary: On every moved block of a snap that the run does not evaluate off its snap, the device measures the snapped family; for a producer's snap of its own emission, what the run concludes from the emission holds of the snapped family there.
A-SNAP.title: The device measures the snapped family where the run reads the snap
A-SNAP.user_statement: Applies only where the run record names blocks as resting on it, a premise about your device. The engine moves each measurement onto its numerical lattice. Where it holds a reference of your model, it computes the key rate on the model at the points the moved measurement found; where the reported rate was formed there, the blocks carrying the reference do not rest on this. On the named blocks, the key rate is computed as if the device performed the moved measurement. It may treat as possible an outcome your model treats as impossible, except in rows and columns the record states to be exactly zero; on a block flagged support_not_preserved, not even there. The engine cannot check this. The record names the cause and a fix: a model with a reference, a run that uses enclosed references, the reasons the reference's bound was not counted or certified, or your device's loss and dark counts.
A-SNAP.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

A-SPEC.summary: Declared dimensions, alphabets, tables and measurements describe the apparatus: the receiver's in every round whatever the others did and, where no source certificate is demanded, Alice's of two or more letters; every input yields a key. The compiler checks only the last, in part.
A-SPEC.title: Specification faithful to the apparatus
A-SPEC.user_statement: Your declared numbers describe your apparatus: each system has its declared dimension, every alphabet and table (announcements, sifting, the raw key bit) is what your devices and software do, and the key rule yields a key value, never "no key", on every input. Each measuring station, of either party, performs exactly its declared measurement in every round, on that round's input alone; afterpulsing or a dead time violates this. A declared receiver instrument's measurement is the model the engine emits from it; the emission step is recorded, not bounded. Where no source-replacement certificate is demanded (an untrusted source, or a one-dimensional A), Alice's declared measurement of her letter is the one she performs; [[A-ALICE-MEAS]] adds every round, alone. The engine checks that the declaration is well formed, not that it matches your hardware.
A-SPEC.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.meat-core: trusted-source mode at d_A >= 2, on a run that reports a key length or a first-order bound; vacuous at d_A = 1 and never demanded there
emission.protocol-compiler: read off the transmitter artefact's own ledger

A-SRC.summary: In trusted-source mode the retained system A stays in the laboratory of the party that holds it and is acted on only by that party's declared measurement, condition (SR3) of the certificate. It is what lets a declared marginal delete attacks.
A-SRC.title: Retention of the system A in trusted-source mode
A-SRC.user_statement: The source's retained half, system A, never leaves the laboratory of the party the declaration assigns it to, and nothing acts on it except that party's own declared measurement: no other step of the protocol and no action of the adversary. In a prepare-and-measure setup A exists only in the source-replacement description, and this is the premise that the adversary has no access to that party's laboratory. Only then may you declare the source's reduced state τ_A (trusted-source mode), which removes attacks from the analysis when A has dimension at least two. If you cannot vouch for this, use untrusted-source mode: the key rate can only drop, and the result stays valid.
A-SRC.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

A-THRESH.summary: Each detector reports one bit per gate, with no photon-number resolution, no memory or timing effects, and no correlations beyond the declared dark-count channel. It fixes the click-or-no-click outcome alphabet the receiver's measurement is built on.
A-THRESH.title: Threshold detectors without memory
A-THRESH.user_statement: Your detectors are threshold (click or no-click) detectors read once per gate. They have no photon-number resolution, no dead time, no afterpulsing and no timing jitter. Gates and detectors are correlated only through the dark-count model you declared. Dark counts are independent from round to round, and between detectors unless you declared a correlated dark-count channel. Detectors with dead time or afterpulsing at your gate rate violate this.
A-THRESH.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

A-TRUST.summary: The declared instrument describes the physical receiver exactly, and the receiver is under the legitimate party's control. It is the parent of most of the receiver's device assumptions, which spell out its parts.
A-TRUST.title: Trusted and exactly characterised receiver
A-TRUST.user_statement: The receiver you declared is the receiver you run. Its mode space, its optical layout (or the instrument or Gram matrices you supplied), the assignment of outputs to detectors, the efficiencies, the dark-count probabilities and the probe states are those of the physical device, with no uncertainty to account for. The device is under your control, and nobody else can select, tune or influence it. A characterisation uncertainty is not modelled: the result applies to the device exactly as declared.
A-TRUST.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

emission.reductions: at a station only where its declared setting set T has at least two values, or where the consuming specification applies a public choice at the station's measured factor (a choice-weighted physical family or a choice weighting of that factor, protocol-compiler/def:spec (b), (b')); this module does not hold that specification, so the emission is told whether such a choice is applied, and where it is not told the row is emitted (req:assumption-ledger)

A-TSM.summary: Every per-round public choice of known bias at the measurement the emitted family describes, its private setting included where it has one, is a component of the emitted outcome and enters only through its statistics. No derivation then assumes a state-independent test fraction.
A-TSM.title: Output-state test statistics
A-TSM.user_statement: Every per-round random choice with a known bias made at this station (for example its probe setting, where it has one, or whether a round is a test round, where that is added by relabelling its outcomes) is recorded as part of that round's outcome, and it enters the analysis only through the observed statistics. No derivation of this contract then assumes a state-independent test fraction.
A-TSM.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

A-VAC.summary: Undeclared input modes and dilation modes start in vacuum. A mode that can carry light to a detector is declared, as a channel mode if the adversary can populate it and as a source mode if the legitimate party does.
A-VAC.title: Vacuum on undeclared input modes
A-VAC.user_statement: Every optical input of your receiver that you did not declare as an input, and every internal loss or ancilla mode, receives no light. A mode that can carry light to a detector is declared: as a channel mode if an attacker could put light into it, and as a source mode if your own equipment, for example a probe laser, does.
A-VAC.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

A-WCP.summary: The physical source emits exactly the declared phase-randomised weak coherent state of each round's letter, drawn with its declared weight, in the declared modes only and independently across rounds. It ties the tagged declaration to the device, in the place of [[A-ENS]].
A-WCP.title: Emission of the declared weak-coherent-pulse states
A-WCP.user_statement: Your weak-coherent-pulse source emits, in every round, a fully phase-randomised coherent pulse at exactly the declared intensity μ and polarisation, in the two declared optical modes only, and nothing else; the numbers are those of your tagged declaration, exactly as declared. No other property of the pulse (timing, spectrum, spatial shape) depends on the chosen bit, basis, intensity or round type, and the round type (test or generation) changes nothing emitted. Intensities do not fluctuate. Each round's letter is drawn independently with the declared probabilities, and no round's letter or emitted pulse depends on another round, its detection results or its public messages. Intensity fluctuations, imperfect phase randomisation or pattern effects violate this.
A-WCP.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

foundations/ass:snapped-measurement.summary: On every moved block of a snap that the run does not evaluate off its snap, the device measures the snapped family; for a producer's snap of its own emission, what the run concludes from the emission holds of the snapped family there.
foundations/ass:snapped-measurement.title: The device measures the snapped family where the run reads the snap
foundations/ass:snapped-measurement.user_statement: Applies only where the run record names blocks as resting on it, a premise about your device. The engine moves each measurement onto its numerical lattice. Where it holds a reference of your model, it computes the key rate on the model at the points the moved measurement found; where the reported rate was formed there, the blocks carrying the reference do not rest on this. On the named blocks, the key rate is computed as if the device performed the moved measurement. It may treat as possible an outcome your model treats as impossible, except in rows and columns the record states to be exactly zero; on a block flagged support_not_preserved, not even there. The engine cannot check this. The record names the cause and a fix: a model with a reference, a run that uses enclosed references, the reasons the reference's bound was not counted or certified, or your device's loss and dark counts.

foundations/def:evaluated-off-snap.summary: A declarer hands a reference beside a snap when it passes on the reference's centres and radii with it, unaltered. A block is evaluated off its snap when nothing its key length is computed from reads the snapped block, save the points and the values fixed before the first round.
foundations/def:evaluated-off-snap.title: A reference handed beside a snap; a block evaluated off its snap

foundations/req:snap-reference.summary: A measurement snap keeps the blocks known exactly on the lattice and moves the others by one fidelity-first, support-safe procedure. A moved block not evaluated off its snap rests on the snap premise, recorded with cause, group and fix; the strict option refuses it.
foundations/req:snap-reference.title: Snaps of a measurement family: kept, or moved and disclosed

meat-core/ass:auth.summary: Every classical message travels through an authentication scheme using at most k_auth bits of pre-shared key and realising the authenticated classical channel within ε_auth, a reused key's distance from an ideal one included. It is the premise by which authentication enters the key's security.
meat-core/ass:auth.title: Authentication of the classical channel by a keyed scheme
meat-core/ass:auth.user_statement: Every classical message of your protocol, per-round announcements included, is protected by one authentication scheme: the attacker may read, delay or block any message, but one she alters or injects, or delivers before it was sent, is rejected except within an error ε_auth. It uses at most k_auth bits of pre-shared secret key per run. That error is its composable error on two identical copies of a uniform, independent key plus the distance of the parties' actual copies from such a pair (zero for a fresh key; for a key from an earlier run, a distance you must bound, which that run's security parameter alone does not bound); declare that sum as ε_auth and the bits used as k_auth. No composable proof for this timing-aware channel is published yet; Wegman–Carter authentication with separate keys per direction approximates it. Both declared zero assert a keyless authenticated channel.

meat-core/ass:conform.summary: The implementation applies the acceptance test and the verification abort, sends no message beyond the model's, outputs the model's key or nothing, uses no key before the execution ends and aborts on an authentication failure. It ties the analysed protocol to the one that runs.
meat-core/ass:conform.title: The implementation runs the analysed post-processing
meat-core/ass:conform.user_statement: Your implementation runs exactly the analysed post-processing. It aborts unless the acceptance statistics lie in the declared acceptance set; after the rounds it sends no public message other than the error-correction transcript of at most λ_EC bits and its seed, the verification seed, hash and result, the privacy-amplification hash choice and the closing accept or abort decisions; it aborts when verification fails or a message fails authentication (an auth-abort); it outputs the analysed ℓ-bit key, or nothing. No part of the key is used before the execution has ended: the key holder, having sent its final decision, waits until the partner has received it or an auth-abort in its place, and the partner until one of these has arrived. Interactive error correction, a resent syndrome or early key use violate this. Tightening 2ε_auth to ε_auth under this timing is an open question.

meat-core/ass:eve-dim.summary: Every register of the adversary, her initial register and her memories, is finite-dimensional, with no bound on its dimension. No claim rests on it: the analysed models have such registers by definition, and [[meat-core/cor:composed-security]] reaches an adversary whose memory has any dimension.
meat-core/ass:eve-dim.title: The adversary's registers are finite-dimensional
meat-core/ass:eve-dim.user_statement: No run rests on this assumption: the security statement of a run holds against an attacker whose quantum memory has any size, finite or infinite ([[meat-core/cor:composed-security]]). The assumption states that the attacker's quantum memory is finite-dimensional, of any size she likes.

meat-core/ass:fixed.summary: The acceptance set, the round count, the key length, the transcript length, the error budgets, the authentication parameters and the Rényi order are fixed before the run and applied unchanged. The key length is that of a fixed-length protocol, not one chosen from the run's data.
meat-core/ass:fixed.title: Protocol parameters fixed before the run
meat-core/ass:fixed.user_statement: Every parameter the key length rests on is fixed before the run starts: the acceptance test, the number of rounds, the key length, the error-correction budget λ_EC, the error budgets ε_PA and ε_EV, and the authentication parameters ε_auth and k_auth. The Rényi order α at which the key length is computed is fixed before the run too; choosing it by comparing the key lengths your declared model gives at several orders, as the run tier's outer search over α does, reads no data of the run and is such a choice. None of them may be chosen or adjusted after looking at the run's data, for example by relaxing the acceptance threshold or picking the key length from the observed error rate. That would be a variable-length protocol, which this analysis does not cover.

meat-core/ass:hash.summary: Privacy amplification uses an ideal two-universal family, collision probability exactly 2^−ℓ for distinct inputs, and error verification a two-universal family. The first is what leftover hashing reads, the second what the verification collision bound reads.
meat-core/ass:hash.title: Ideal two-universal privacy amplification
meat-core/ass:hash.user_statement: Privacy amplification uses a hash family in which any two different inputs collide with probability exactly 2^−ℓ (an ideal two-universal family, such as Toeplitz hashing), and error verification uses a two-universal hash family. If your privacy-amplification family is only two-universal (collision probability at most 2^−ℓ), shorten the key by one further bit.

meat-core/ass:keyreg.summary: The post-processing acts on the raw-key string the rounds write, the declared holder computes that string, and reconciliation runs one way from the holder through a padded fixed-length transcript. The leakage term counts the register's full length.
meat-core/ass:keyreg.title: Dedicated key register and one-way reconciliation
meat-core/ass:keyreg.user_statement: Error correction is one-way. The key holder computes its raw key from its own record (its letters, the detection results of its measuring stations, or both, whichever it holds) and the public announcements, and its messages depend only on that raw key and public random seeds. The transcript always has exactly λ_EC bits, shorter messages being padded. Interactive error correction (for example Cascade) or a variable-length transcript is not covered by this key length.

meat-core/ass:lab.summary: Nothing about a party's records leaves its laboratory but its key, the public messages and, in trusted-source mode at the party of A, the emitted systems; the adversary acts on it only through what its declared measurements receive and the messages. It excludes side channels at both parties.
meat-core/ass:lab.title: Each party's laboratory is sealed
meat-core/ass:lab.user_statement: Whatever a party's role, nothing about its letters, settings, choices, detection results, keys or random numbers leaves its laboratory but the final key, the public messages and, where the party sends with a trusted source, the signals that source emits; timing and auxiliary signals reveal no more. An untrusted source counts as outside every laboratory, even one it is in. The attacker reaches a laboratory only via the systems its declared measurements receive and the public messages. Light sent in to read out a letter, a setting, a choice or a detector state (a Trojan-horse attack, at a receiver as at a modulator), emanations from any device, detector back-flash and anything but the declared input modes influencing a measurement violate this, a clock or trigger line from an untrusted source included; where it sends with a trusted source, so does light seeding or recalibrating its laser.

meat-core/ass:seed.summary: The post-processing seeds are drawn with their declared laws, privately, independently and afresh; in trusted-source mode the source's letters and prepared systems are independent of the adversary, who never gets a purification of them. Leftover hashing and source replacement rest on it.
meat-core/ass:seed.title: Private, independent and fresh local randomness
meat-core/ass:seed.user_statement: Your random choices come from a good private random number generator. The error-correction seed, the error-verification hash and the privacy-amplification hash are each drawn with their intended distribution, kept secret until the protocol announces them, independent of each other, of every other record of the protocol (the raw key included) and of everything the attacker knows, and drawn anew in every run. With a trusted source, the randomness with which it picks each round's letter and prepares its state is uncorrelated with the attacker at the start, and no purification of a prepared state is ever available to the attacker. A seed reused across runs, fixed in the device or disclosed early, or a predictable or pre-shared random source, violates this.

meat-core/ass:separate-executions.summary: Several executions, fixed in advance and run against one adversary, touch none of each other's registers, leave their keys unused until all have ended, and keep their own premises with the others counted as the adversary's. It is what lets their security parameters add.
meat-core/ass:separate-executions.title: Executions that share no key and no device state
meat-core/ass:separate-executions.user_statement: You run several executions, one after another or at the same time, and want their security parameters to add. Their number and parameters are fixed before the first starts. Each execution has its own key material, randomness, seeds and pre-shared authentication key, such as a separate part of one pool. No device, memory or random source carries information between them. An execution has ended once both parties have fixed their output, key or abort, after the closing messages; no key is used or read, and nothing else leaks from an ended one, until all have ended. The assumptions each execution's run record lists must still hold when an attacker holds and runs every other execution, her memory, which then holds their systems, of any dimension. A key that authenticates another execution, a key used early, or parameters chosen from an earlier execution's data violate this.

meat-core/cor:composed-security.summary: Secrecy and correctness compose to (ε_PA + ε_EV)-security with honest authentication; over an authentication scheme within ε_auth that consumes k_auth bits of pre-shared key, the protocol is (ε_PA + ε_EV + 2ε_auth)-secure; when both parties output a key, its net key gain is ℓ − k_auth bits.
meat-core/cor:composed-security.title: Security of the protocol and its net key
meat-core/cor:composed-security.user_statement: A run either aborts or outputs a key of ℓ bits that is a perfect key up to the security parameter ε: identical for both parties, uniform and independent of all the attacker holds, public messages included. One party may abort while the other gets a key. No test, whatever the attacker knows, tells the run's output from an ideal protocol's with advantage above ε = ε_PA + ε_EV + 2ε_auth. It holds against every attack, of any memory, if every premise in the run record holds, [[A-AUTH]], [[A-CONFORM]] and [[A-FIXED]] included. A first-order run also needs its bound to hold, computed h_lb ≤ h_low, which no premise covers ([[meat-core/frank-wolfe/rem:fo-arithmetic]]). ε averages over aborted runs too. The criterion is composable. Separate executions provably add ε ([[meat-core/cor:separate-executions]]). Not every later use of the key is covered ([[meat-core/rem:repeated-executions]]). A run where both get a key nets ℓ − k_auth bits; an abort uses up to k_auth. Abort rates: [[meat-core/rem:completeness-scope]].

meat-core/cor:keylength-bound.summary: Any h ≤ h_low may replace h_low in the key-length bound through max{0, h}, with the same security statement. This is where every solver obtains its key length; a bound h ≤ 0 yields no positive key when ε_EV < 1.
meat-core/cor:keylength-bound.title: Key length from any lower bound on the value

meat-core/cor:separate-executions.summary: N executions that share no key and no device state and leave their keys unused until all have ended, run against one adversary, are together (ε_1 + ... + ε_N)-secure for the joint ideal map. A key reused from one execution in another is not covered.
meat-core/cor:separate-executions.title: Security parameters of separate executions add
meat-core/cor:separate-executions.user_statement: Running several executions against the same attacker, one after another or at the same time, costs the sum of their security parameters. If each execution i is secure with parameter ε_i and [[A-SEPARATE]] holds, whose conditions include that their number and parameters are fixed before the first starts, that they share no key material and no device state, and that their keys stay unused until all have ended, then all their keys together are within ε_1 + ... + ε_N of independent ideal keys. Parameters chosen from an earlier execution's data are not covered, nor is a key from one execution reused in another, for example to authenticate it.

meat-core/def:admissible-declaration.summary: An admissible declaration is finite with total maps, a well-formed marginal slot, block-diagonal POVMs, announcement-determined sifting, constraints typed by the source mode and a non-empty feasible set. Each party announces from its own readout and the key holder computes the raw key from its own.
meat-core/def:admissible-declaration.title: Admissible declaration

meat-core/def:declaration.summary: The declaration is the compiler's ([[protocol-compiler/def:declaration]]), in either format, admissible ([[meat-core/def:admissible-declaration]]), sifting by the announcements and a raw key its holder can compute. This module adds the key-live acceptance values, its reading of the party partition, the summation order and exact admissibility.
meat-core/def:declaration.title: The protocol declaration as the MEAT core reads it

meat-core/def:dropped.summary: A run may give up the entropy of chosen pairs of a key-live acceptance value and a joint sector by setting their deficits to zero, keeping every variable, statistic and constraint. The result is a program of its own; once any pair is dropped, its value is never reported as the undropped one.
meat-core/def:dropped.title: Dropped set and dropped program

meat-core/frank-wolfe/ass:lmo.summary: At every iterate a first-order bound uses, the block list consumed from the oracle, any positivity repair included, puts the linear form of the gradient its bracket consumes at or below its minimum over the exact Choi feasible set. No claim rests on it: [[meat-core/frank-wolfe/lem:feasible-side-dual]] bounds that minimum instead.
meat-core/frank-wolfe/ass:lmo.title: Exact linear minimisation over the feasible set
meat-core/frank-wolfe/ass:lmo.user_statement: No run rests on this assumption: the engine verifies a lower bound on the solver's linear minimisation in exact arithmetic instead of trusting it. The assumption states that at every step whose bound the engine uses, the semidefinite-programming solver returned a block list at which the linear objective it was asked to minimise, the gradient of the objective the bound is taken for, is no larger than its true minimum over the exact feasible set, after the engine's small positivity repair of the return.

meat-core/frank-wolfe/cor:certified-keyl.summary: The largest bracket formed by [[meat-core/frank-wolfe/lem:certified-bracket]] over finitely many points is a first-order bound of [[meat-core/frank-wolfe/thm:firstorder]], so it is at most the value of the declaration it is formed on and gives that declaration's fixed-length key length exactly as h_lb does.
meat-core/frank-wolfe/cor:certified-keyl.title: Key length from the certified bracket
meat-core/frank-wolfe/cor:certified-keyl.user_statement: The certified key rate is the best of a few brackets, each formed from enclosures of the gradient at a point the search found, with every arithmetic step from the declaration's data exact or rigorously enclosed. It is a lower bound on the minimum h_low of the declaration it is formed on, and the key length built from it is secret and correct under the same premises as the first-order key length: the declaration's modelling premises remain, but no premise about how a number was computed is added, the key length itself being computed exactly, its one logarithm enclosed until the integer part is decided. It is not a bound on any other declaration, so a run formed on the snapped declaration still rests where its record says on the premise that the device measures the snapped family.

meat-core/frank-wolfe/cor:certified-keyl.summary: On a reference companion, the best certified bracket, formed over its enclosed measured family as [[meat-core/frank-wolfe/lem:certified-bracket-enclosed]] allows, gives the key length of the protocol whose declaration is the companion, as the first-order bound on the companion does.
meat-core/frank-wolfe/cor:certified-keyl.title: Key length on a reference companion from the certified bracket

meat-core/frank-wolfe/cor:fo-dropped.summary: In either source mode the first-order bound holds for the dropped program ([[meat-core/def:dropped]]), with maximal support asked only of key-active pairs (acceptance value, joint sector) whose entropy is kept. It bounds h_low from below, also at iterates feasible only up to windows.
meat-core/frank-wolfe/cor:fo-dropped.title: First-order bound for the dropped program

meat-core/frank-wolfe/cor:fo-reference.summary: At any points, such as those of a search on the snapped declaration or of one continued on the companion, the bracket formed with the reference companion's objective, gradient, entries and linear minima bounds the companion's value from below; its key length is the reference model's.
meat-core/frank-wolfe/cor:fo-reference.title: The first-order bound on the reference companion

meat-core/frank-wolfe/lem:certified-brac.summary: At a point with positive definite blocks and positive probabilities the gradient paired with the point is the objective, so the bracket is the sum of its two lower bounds and needs only enclosures of the gradient.
meat-core/frank-wolfe/lem:certified-brac.title: The certified bracket from enclosures of the gradient

meat-core/frank-wolfe/lem:certified-brac.summary: Over a reference companion whose measured families, of one or more replaced factors, are known through entrywise enclosures and on some blocks enclosed factors, one enclosure of the gradient serves the companion where every element the gradient reads has its zero pattern and rank fixed.
meat-core/frank-wolfe/lem:certified-brac.title: The certified bracket over a measured family known through enclosures

meat-core/frank-wolfe/lem:feasible-side-.summary: Any multipliers for the coupling condition and the declared rows give a lower bound on a linear form's minimum over the exact Choi feasible set, dual-feasible or not, since the coupling fixes every feasible point's total trace. Rows built from an inexact frame cost an explicit deduction.
meat-core/frank-wolfe/lem:feasible-side-.title: A lower bound on the feasible-side minimum from any multipliers

meat-core/frank-wolfe/rem:certified-scop.summary: A certified number rests on the claims, the modelling premises of its declaration and the correctness of the code, its ball-arithmetic library included, and on no premise about arithmetic. It does not reach data computed before the declaration; a receiver weight in floating point withholds it.
meat-core/frank-wolfe/rem:certified-scop.title: What a certified number rests on
meat-core/frank-wolfe/rem:certified-scop.user_statement: Certified means that every number between the declaration and the key rate was computed exactly or with a rigorous bound on its rounding. It does not mean that the declaration describes your devices: the source, receiver and laboratory premises in the report still apply, and a number formed on the snapped measurement rests where the record says on the device measuring it. Nor is the software assumed correct by a premise: its correctness, its interval-arithmetic library included, is checked by review and tests. Ideal analysers with irrational projector entries (at pi/8, say) certify on your model where the receiver gives their elements in factor form; otherwise, as for some lossy multi-photon receivers, the rate can be certified on the snapped measurement, resting there on that premise, unless the run sets strict_snaps. A floating-point multiclick weight keeps the first-order number.

meat-core/frank-wolfe/rem:fo-arithmetic.summary: Both linear minima are bounded exactly over the exact sets, but for the gradient as computed: the objective, the gradient and the maps and frame behind them are binary64, and a reference's centres move the measured family. So a computed h_lb may exceed h_low, and the zero clamp repairs neither.
meat-core/frank-wolfe/rem:fo-arithmetic.title: Exact real arithmetic in the first-order bound

meat-core/frank-wolfe/rem:fo-interface.summary: A run reports its estimate always, and h_lb only where the hypotheses of [[meat-core/frank-wolfe/thm:firstorder]] held, membership of the consumed point in the acceptance set times the relaxed set among them. No hypothesis is read of the solver, and withdrawal never weakens what h_lb means.
meat-core/frank-wolfe/rem:fo-interface.title: Two reported numbers and one first-order claim

meat-core/frank-wolfe/req:bracket-on-ref.summary: Where a reference companion is admitted, the run's first-order number is the best bracket on the companion at the best points of the snapped search and of a short search continued on the companion from them, each assessed by the usual gate; the snapped bound is recorded as a diagnostic only.
meat-core/frank-wolfe/req:bracket-on-ref.title: The first-order bound evaluated on the reference companion

meat-core/frank-wolfe/req:certified-eval.summary: The engine forms the bracket again at the final points, every step exact or rigorously enclosed, and reports the best at the certified tier; if a companion certifies none, on the searched declaration under [[A-SNAP]] unless strict_snaps is set. Else the first-order number stays, or a strict run refuses.
meat-core/frank-wolfe/req:certified-eval.title: The certified evaluation of the first-order bound
meat-core/frank-wolfe/req:certified-eval.user_statement: After the search, the engine recomputes the bound at the few points the reported number came from, in an arithmetic that encloses every rounding, from the declaration's data. Where that succeeds at some point, the key rate is certified: no step between the declaration and the number rests on floating-point arithmetic being accurate enough.
