Where it fails on the model the engine holds of your device, it is tried again on the moved measurement the search ran on, unless the run sets strict_snaps; a rate certified there is reported as certified, and the report names the premise that your device performs the moved measurement on the blocks concerned ([[A-SNAP]]). Where both fail, for instance because a detector element has a rank no enclosure fixes or a multiclick weight was computed in floating point, the report keeps the first-order number and says why; a strict run is refused instead.

meat-core/frank-wolfe/req:first-order-wi.summary: An iterate at which a first-order hypothesis fails or is not established contributes no bracket and its reason is recorded; with none left h_lb is withdrawn and the run falls to the estimate tier. The oracle's return and its status withdraw nothing.
meat-core/frank-wolfe/req:first-order-wi.title: Withdrawal of the first-order bound

meat-core/frank-wolfe/thm:firstorder.summary: In exact real arithmetic the best linearisation over the iterates, even ones feasible only up to windows, bounds h_low from below given positive probabilities, maximal branch support, unperturbed gradients and bounds on both linear minima. An exactly feasible point's objective bounds it from above.
meat-core/frank-wolfe/thm:firstorder.title: The estimate and the first-order lower bound
meat-core/frank-wolfe/thm:firstorder.user_statement: The headline key rate rests on this bound, which needs no exact optimum. The per-round bound h_low is the minimum of a convex optimisation. At each step whose positivity and full-support conditions hold, the tangent plane of the objective lies below it over the feasible set, so its lowest point bounds h_low from below; the engine reports the best such bound, h_lb. That point is bounded without trusting a solver: one part is computed exactly, the other verified in exact arithmetic from the solver's dual against the exact constraint rows, the floating-point frame W_t's error in those rows deducted. The engine evaluates the objective, its gradient and the maps and frame they are built from in floating point, with no error budget, so a computed h_lb can exceed h_low by an amount no claim bounds. Its points are feasible only within a window, so its reported estimate need not lie above h_low.

meat-core/lem:estimate.summary: The objective at any exactly feasible point, a state or the Choi operators of [[meat-core/thm:choi]] that parametrise one, is at least the value h_low of the program. It warrants the estimate every run reports, a solver diagnostic and never the lower bound a key length needs.
meat-core/lem:estimate.title: Upper estimate of the value at any feasible point

meat-core/lem:ev-correctness.summary: In the fixed-length post-processing model the two parties accept with different keys with probability at most ε_EV, for every attack and every output length. It is the correctness half of the protocol's security.
meat-core/lem:ev-correctness.title: Correctness from error verification
meat-core/lem:ev-correctness.user_statement: This is the correctness half of security. Before the key is formed, the key holder announces a ⌈log₂(1/ε_EV)⌉-bit hash of its raw key, computed with a hash function drawn at random independently of the raw keys, and the partner compares it with the hash of its own corrected copy; a mismatch aborts the run. Two different raw keys pass only through a hash collision, so the chance that both parties accept yet hold different keys is at most ε_EV, whatever the attacker does and whatever key length you choose. It needs a two-universal hash family ([[A-HASH]]), seeds independent of the raw keys ([[A-SEED]]) and an implementation that aborts as specified ([[A-CONFORM]]), and takes messages to arrive unaltered; [[meat-core/cor:composed-security]] adds real authentication. It does not promise that error correction succeeds, only that a failure is caught, except with probability ε_EV.

meat-core/prop:minimal-divergence.summary: Dropping every pair leaves α/(α−1) times the minimal divergence between accepted distributions and feasible statistics, and h_low lies between that and it plus log₂(d_Z+1) times the key-live mass. A positive lower bound proves that no feasible state has accepted statistics.
meat-core/prop:minimal-divergence.title: The minimal divergence as the value with every pair dropped
meat-core/prop:minimal-divergence.user_statement: The key-rate program charges a penalty whenever the accepted statistics differ from the per-round statistics of every state the declared devices admit. This result isolates that penalty. If some such state has statistics the acceptance test accepts, the program's value is at most the entropy ceiling, log₂(d_Z+1) times the largest key-live probability an accepted distribution gives. If none has, the value has a floor that grows without limit as the Rényi order approaches one, so a key length can grow with the mismatch rather than with the secrecy of the key. A positive lower bound on the penalty-only program, which the engine computes with its usual solver, proves that no such state has accepted per-round statistics. It does not prove that a finite run of those devices fails the test: its frequencies can still fall in the acceptance set.

meat-core/prop:model-pass-bound.summary: If every round's acceptance value, given the earlier ones, follows the statistics of a feasible state, the run passes the acceptance test with probability at most 2^(−n D_min). A lower bound b at one order thus caps that probability at 2^(−n (α₀−1)/α₀ · b).
meat-core/prop:model-pass-bound.title: The pass probability of devices the declared model admits
meat-core/prop:model-pass-bound.user_statement: This result bounds how often devices that behave as your declared model says would pass your acceptance test. Suppose that in every round, given what happened before, the acceptance value is distributed as the statistics of some state the declaration admits as feasible. Then the run passes the test with probability at most 2^(−n D_min), where D_min is the minimal divergence of [[meat-core/prop:minimal-divergence]], and the engine's proven lower bound on D_min gives a computable cap. This is a statement about the declared model, not about your real devices and not about an attacker. If the acceptance set was fixed before the run, the cap is tiny and your real devices do pass, that is evidence at the level of the cap, not a proof, that the model does not describe them ([[statistics/ass:reach]]). A set built from the same run's frequencies passes by construction.

meat-core/prop:optol-nobound.summary: Two exactly admissible measurements on Q within ϵ of each other can have rate bounds α/(α−1)·N bits per round apart, for every positive integer N ≤ 53 + log₂ϵ (up to 52). So closeness of the declared measurement cannot be relied on to carry a key-rate claim to a nearby declaration.
meat-core/prop:optol-nobound.title: Instability of the rate under measurement perturbations

meat-core/prop:value-range.summary: The objective is non-negative on the feasible set, so h_low lies in [0, +∞]; each entropy term is at most log₂(d_Z + 1), while the divergence penalty has no finite bound. If h_low = +∞, no accepted distribution is absolutely continuous with respect to the statistics of a feasible state.
meat-core/prop:value-range.title: Range of the value and its finite entropy part

meat-core/rem:completeness-scope.summary: The completeness parameter ε* of the statistics module bounds an honest run's failure of the acceptance test only. Aborts in error verification and in authentication are bounded by no claim, so ε* does not bound the honest abort probability of the whole protocol.
meat-core/rem:completeness-scope.title: Completeness covers the acceptance test only
meat-core/rem:completeness-scope.user_statement: The completeness figure ε* bounds one thing only: the chance that an honest run, with no attacker and devices behaving as the declared honest model says, fails the acceptance test on its statistics. An honest run can also abort later: in error verification, when error correction leaves the two raw keys different, and in authentication. No result bounds those aborts, so an honest run's overall abort chance can exceed ε*. Whether your error-correction code reconstructs the key on honest runs is yours to check; it affects only how often you obtain a key. Completeness never affects the security parameter ε, which holds for every abort pattern ([[meat-core/cor:composed-security]]) and so says nothing about how often runs abort.

meat-core/rem:declared-measurement.summary: A tiny change of the declared measurement can move the key rate by many bits per round, so the model is a premise of the rate. Where a handed reference's companion counts and the key length is formed on it, the snap only steers the search; nothing bounds model to device.
meat-core/rem:declared-measurement.title: The declared measurement as a premise of the rate
meat-core/rem:declared-measurement.user_statement: The key rate is computed from the measurement model you declare for your receiver, and that model is a premise of the number: nothing checks that your device measures what it says (for a receiver the engine models, [[A-TRUST]]). A change of the model too small to see in its entries, notably one that makes an outcome nearly or exactly impossible, can move the rate by many bits per round in either direction; no result bounds that gap. The engine also moves your model onto its exact number grid (the snap) for its search. Where your model reaches the engine as a reference, the bound is evaluated on your model itself and needs no premise about the snap, unless the rate is certified only on the moved model, as the report then says; any other block rests on [[A-SNAP]], or the run refuses if it declares the strict option. Validate the model, above all which outcomes it treats as impossible.

meat-core/rem:plus2.summary: The key-length bound carries the constant +1 where its source derivation and the published fixed-length statement carry +2: one announced bit buys secrecy on the accepted state by an elementary contraction. The source's secrecy definition, conditioned on the acceptance test alone, does not spend it.
meat-core/rem:plus2.title: The constant in the key length and the source's convention

meat-core/rem:repeated-executions.summary: One execution's parameter covers one run, and separate executions that share no key add their parameters ([[meat-core/cor:separate-executions]]). A reused authentication key enters through ε_auth, charged twice, and the earlier run's parameter does not bound its distance in general.
meat-core/rem:repeated-executions.title: One execution's security parameter and a reused key
meat-core/rem:repeated-executions.user_statement: The security parameter ε covers one execution: one run of n rounds and its post-processing. It is not a per-round or per-bit figure, and it does not shrink when you repeat the protocol. Several executions are together secure with the sum of their ε ([[meat-core/cor:separate-executions]]) under [[A-SEPARATE]]. The sum does not cover parameters chosen from an earlier run's data, such as the error-correction budget or the acceptance test. The conditions of [[A-SEPARATE]] include: (i) their number and parameters are all fixed before the first starts; (ii) they share no key material and no device state; (iii) their keys stay unused until the last has ended. Reusing key from an earlier run to authenticate the next is not covered either. Such a key enters only through the next run's declared authentication error ε_auth, counted twice, and the earlier run's ε does not by itself bound how far that key is from an ideal one.

meat-core/req:constrained-key-gate.summary: A key length is emitted with a non-empty constraint list only if the list is licensed for the declared source mode and the attack-set licence is present. Otherwise the request is refused, and the numbers serve only for exploration.
meat-core/req:constrained-key-gate.title: Two-part gate on a key length with declared constraints

meat-core/req:exact-admission.summary: The engine admits a declaration only if it is exactly admissible and refuses every other, with no tolerance on declared data, save a reference companion, admitted on its own terms. [[meat-core/prop:optol-nobound]] shows, for the measurement on Q, that closeness to admissible data could license no key-length claim.
meat-core/req:exact-admission.title: Exact admission of declared data

meat-core/req:hash-penalty.summary: For a privacy-amplification family that is only two-universal, collision probability at most 2^−ℓ, the key-length bound is tightened by one further bit, ℓ → ℓ − 1.
meat-core/req:hash-penalty.title: Key-length penalty for a merely two-universal family

meat-core/req:key-length-alpha-domain.summary: The engine reports a key length only at a Rényi order α in (1, 2), the order at which every key-length statement holds, and reports none at any other order.
meat-core/req:key-length-alpha-domain.title: Rényi order of a reported key length

meat-core/req:marginal-licence-gate.summary: A declared trusted marginal without the source-replacement licence is refused before any key-length output. At a one-dimensional Alice system the licence is vacuous and is not demanded.
meat-core/req:marginal-licence-gate.title: Source licence for a declared marginal

meat-core/req:reported-key-length.summary: The engine reports the maximal key length built from the lower bound h on h_low it uses, the right-hand side of the key-length bound at max{0, h} floored and clamped at 0, as its conservative integer output.
meat-core/req:reported-key-length.title: Reported key length

meat-core/req:security-statement-not-vac.summary: The engine refuses a run whose budgets satisfy ε_PA + ε_EV + 2ε_auth ≥ 1, deciding the sum exactly on the three declared numbers before any program is built. The security statement of [[meat-core/cor:composed-security]] is then empty, and [[meat-core/cor:keylength-bound]] (b) does not claim the corner.
meat-core/req:security-statement-not-vac.title: Refusal of budgets with an empty security statement

meat-core/req:unreachable-acceptance-set.summary: On a checked run the engine bounds the penalty-only value once, before any order is evaluated, and records the cap on the probability that devices as declared pass the acceptance test, proven where b is certified. A run whose cap is at most a threshold, one half by default, is refused.
meat-core/req:unreachable-acceptance-set.title: The check of the acceptance set against the feasible statistics
meat-core/req:unreachable-acceptance-set.user_statement: If you supply the honest statistics or declare a constraint, the engine checks, unless switched off, whether a state the declaration admits has statistics the test accepts. Once per run, before any key length is computed and with a bounded share of one evaluation's time, it bounds the mismatch from below; a short solve can leave a mismatch unproven. From a positive bound it forms a cap on the probability that devices behaving as the declaration says pass your acceptance test, proven where the bound is certified, and the record and report show that cap as a probability. Where the cap is at most one half (adjustable), the model's own devices would fail the test at least as often as pass it, and the run is refused with no key length. The record says whether the run was checked.

meat-core/thm:choi.summary: In trusted-source mode the program is exactly a jointly convex minimisation over sector Choi blocks, with one coupling constraint per Alice sector and affine or conic rows. Every support frame gives the value h_low, since only surjectivity of the parametrisation enters it.
meat-core/thm:choi.title: The Choi program

meat-core/thm:constrained-accumulation.summary: Under the attack-set licence [[A-ATK]], the accumulated entropy bound holds with the constrained single-round rate of a licensed list in place of the unconstrained rate, with the same acceptance-probability penalty. The constrained rate is never below the unconstrained one.
meat-core/thm:constrained-accumulation.title: Constrained accumulation under the attack-set licence

meat-core/thm:keylength.summary: For a Rényi order α in (1, 2), a key of length ℓ ≤ n·h_low − λ_EC − ⌈log₂(1/ε_EV)⌉ − α/(α−1)·log₂(1/ε_PA) + 1 is ε_PA-secret on the accepted state at every all-at-once finite-register attack the reduction chain carries onto the round model ([[A-LINK]]). [[meat-core/cor:composed-security]] extends it to every attack.
meat-core/thm:keylength.title: Secrecy of the key from the accumulated entropy
meat-core/thm:keylength.user_statement: Over n rounds the attacker's uncertainty about the raw key accumulates to n times the per-round bound h_low, less a term for how unlikely the acceptance test is to pass, which cancels over all runs; the bound h_low holds over every attack compatible with your declared devices and with passing statistics. Subtracted are the error-correction transcript of λ_EC bits, the verification hash of ⌈log₂(1/ε_EV)⌉ bits and a finite-size penalty of α/(α−1)·log₂(1/ε_PA) bits; one bit is added back. The remaining key of ℓ bits is secret, counted over all runs: it is within the secrecy parameter ε_PA of a uniform key independent of the attacker's memory and every public message. It is proved for a finite-memory attacker receiving every signal at once; [[meat-core/cor:composed-security]] covers every attacker. The Rényi order α in (1, 2) is fixed before the run ([[A-FIXED]]) and changes the key's length, never its secrecy.

protocol-compiler/ass:alice-meas.summary: Where no source-replacement certificate is demanded, in untrusted-source mode or at d_A = 1, and at least two letters are declared, Alice's letter in every round is the outcome of her declared measurement on that round's system A alone, whatever happens in the other rounds.
protocol-compiler/ass:alice-meas.title: Alice's declared measurement where no source certificate is demanded
protocol-compiler/ass:alice-meas.user_statement: Applies where no source-replacement certificate is demanded and at least two letters are declared. Where the system A is one-dimensional, the declared measurement is only the probabilities of Alice's letter, which is then her local randomness; with a trusted source the engine refuses letter probabilities that differ from the source's and a sent state that depends on the letter. With an untrusted source and A of dimension two or more, Alice measures at her station the system A she receives. In every round she obtains her letter by the same declared measurement on that round's system alone, whatever happens in other rounds, their outcomes and the public messages included. Systems from an untrusted source, being the adversary's, may be correlated across rounds. A device of Alice's declared as a measured factor is a receiver measurement of the specification, not covered here.

protocol-compiler/ass:atk.summary: For a licensed non-empty constraint list that backs a key-length claim, its producer's reduction represents every physical attack with finite registers and every signal at its first channel by an admissible attack sequence. It lets constraints restrict the attacks considered.
protocol-compiler/ass:atk.title: Attack-set licence
protocol-compiler/ass:atk.user_statement: Applies only where constraints restrict the attacks the analysis considers, each in the form your declared source mode admits, which the engine checks. Whoever produced the reduction chain has proved that every attack on your physical system becomes, after the reduction, an attack that respects every listed constraint in every round. The proof is asked of attacks with a finite-dimensional memory, of any size, that receive every signal at the start; the engine extends the security statement to every other attack by a limit ([[meat-core/cor:composed-security]]). For constraints the reductions module produces and certifies, that proof is its licence theorem. A constraint you add yourself, or one supplied without such a certificate, needs that proof from you, or must be removed; the analysis without constraints stays valid.

protocol-compiler/ass:coin.summary: Every public choice is drawn with its declared bias; those of fixed bias are jointly independent of each other, the quantum systems and the adversary, and one weighted by a station's setting depends on the round through that setting only. It lets a weight inside the measurement describe the round.
protocol-compiler/ass:coin.title: Public choices as private coins of declared bias
protocol-compiler/ass:coin.user_statement: Every public choice of your protocol (for example an actively chosen basis, or whether a round is a test round; a basis set passively by a beam splitter is part of the measurement, not a choice), whichever party draws it and at whichever of its stations, comes from a local random number generator with exactly the declared probabilities, and each is announced or kept secret exactly as declared. The choices with fixed probabilities are independent of each other and, all together, of the quantum signals and of anything an attacker does. A choice whose probabilities depend on a station's private setting is drawn by a party whose recorded outcome includes that setting, and may depend on that setting only, never otherwise on Alice's letter, another choice or a detection result.

protocol-compiler/ass:ideal.summary: On the Band-A route the declared receiver is an exactly projective qubit measurement with unit efficiency and no loss, dark counts, multi-photon events or misalignment, on a transmitted system that is exactly a qubit. The route is an explicit idealization, not a squashing argument.
protocol-compiler/ass:ideal.title: Ideal qubit receiver on the Band-A route
protocol-compiler/ass:ideal.user_statement: Only for an idealised Band-A analysis: your receiver is a perfect qubit measurement, with unit detection efficiency, no loss, no dark counts, no multi-photon events and no misalignment, and what reaches it in each round is exactly one qubit. The engine refuses a Band-A declaration whose own numbers contradict this: more than one measuring station, a measured system (or, with a trusted source, a transmitted system) of dimension other than two, or a measurement not made of projectors (per basis, where a basis choice is declared). No real optical receiver meets this; use the route to reproduce textbook comparison values. Declare a real device through the receiver module and a squashing reduction.

protocol-compiler/ass:link.summary: Every link of the reduction chain is sound: its channel exists and is a channel, the reduced protocol's security implies the physical one's, and every transported constraint holds on reachable states. A decided pullback or source identity is a necessary condition only, never this obligation.
protocol-compiler/ass:link.title: Soundness of every reduction link
protocol-compiler/ass:link.user_statement: Every reduction step between your physical devices and the finite model the engine solves is sound, and so is their combination. Each step's channel exists, a channel supplied as numbers is a genuine quantum channel, and a receiver step maps the model's measurement back to the physical one. Security of the reduced protocol implies security of the physical one, and every constraint a step passes on holds for every state an attacker can reach. The run lists this premise wherever it cannot point to a proof: it is not listed on the idealised Band-A route, whose one step is checked to be the identity, nor where every measuring device's single reduction step was built in this run by the engine's reductions module with status exact, with no source step and outcomes kept as they are, where that module's theorems prove it. A chain or channel from elsewhere must come with the proof.

protocol-compiler/ass:rhom.summary: The same specification, source mode and operators describe every round: the sameness clause of round homogeneity, not the absence of memory across rounds. One compiled declaration and one certificate decision then serve the whole run.
protocol-compiler/ass:rhom.title: Round homogeneity of the declaration
protocol-compiler/ass:rhom.user_statement: One protocol description covers the whole run. Every round uses the same measurements, the same setting choices and their probabilities, and the same classical processing, and, where the source is trusted, the same source, so one declaration and one certificate decision apply to all n rounds. A run in which you change settings, or your devices drift so that later rounds need different operators, violates this. Only parts of a run fixed before it starts, each processed as its own execution and composed under [[A-SEPARATE]], which also asks that no device carry a state from one part into the next, can be analysed separately; a split chosen after seeing the data is not covered. That no device remembers earlier rounds is not part of this premise: for the measuring stations it is [[A-SPEC]], for Alice's letter [[A-ALICE-MEAS]], and where the source is trusted the source premise.

protocol-compiler/ass:spec.summary: Declared dimensions, alphabets, tables and measurements describe the apparatus: the receiver's in every round whatever the others did and, where no source certificate is demanded, Alice's of two or more letters; every input yields a key. The compiler checks only the last, in part.
protocol-compiler/ass:spec.title: Specification faithful to the apparatus
protocol-compiler/ass:spec.user_statement: Your declared numbers describe your apparatus: each system has its declared dimension, every alphabet and table (announcements, sifting, the raw key bit) is what your devices and software do, and the key rule yields a key value, never "no key", on every input. Each measuring station, of either party, performs exactly its declared measurement in every round, on that round's input alone; afterpulsing or a dead time violates this. A declared receiver instrument's measurement is the model the engine emits from it; the emission step is recorded, not bounded. Where no source-replacement certificate is demanded (an untrusted source, or a one-dimensional A), Alice's declared measurement of her letter is the one she performs; [[A-ALICE-MEAS]] adds every round, alone. The engine checks that the declaration is well formed, not that it matches your hardware.

protocol-compiler/def:declaration.summary: A protocol declaration fixes the systems, sector map, marginal slot, both measurements, public maps, raw-key map and a typed constraint list, operators on the measured system being block lists. The general format adds factors, Alice sectors, an ensemble form, a transcript and scoped entries.
protocol-compiler/def:declaration.title: Protocol declaration

protocol-compiler/def:well-formed-spec.summary: A specification is well-formed when its declared data are as declared: finite alphabets and systems, total tables, exactly admissible measurement families, the presented physical one included, normalised weights and Hermitian, tagged constraint blocks. The compiler decides every clause.
protocol-compiler/def:well-formed-spec.title: Well-formed specification

protocol-compiler/req:link-row-provenanc.summary: The ledger omits [[A-LINK]] only on Band A and where every measured factor's receiver segment is the single exact instance link of a reductions artefact of the same run, with the identity outcome correspondence. That provenance is the run's, never read from the specification.
protocol-compiler/req:link-row-provenanc.title: Omission of the link-soundness row only on a proved chain

protocol-compiler/thm:band-a.summary: On the direct one-sector route every chain condition but the receiver family's exact admissibility holds by inspection, and the identity link, which delivers the declared measurement, is sound by exhibition. The receiver's residual physical content is the ideal-receiver assumption.
protocol-compiler/thm:band-a.title: The Band-A route

protocol-compiler/thm:chain-consumption.summary: Chain conditions are decided by finite computation; a verified pullback identity reproduces the coarse-grained physical statistics and a verified source identity maps the virtual source onto the specified one. Link soundness and attack-set licences stay obligations this theorem does not discharge.
protocol-compiler/thm:chain-consumption.title: Decided identities and named obligations of a consumed chain

protocol-compiler/thm:choice-encoding.summary: A public choice of known bias enters as weights inside the measurement operators: the family stays a POVM, fixed weights are reproduced exactly as choice probabilities where the weighted family is emitted, and setting-dependent weights commute with the chain. A fraction outside them is refused.
protocol-compiler/thm:choice-encoding.title: Encoding of public choices in the measurement operators

protocol-compiler/thm:gates.summary: Each gate is decidable or a presence test, and each failure has one fixed outcome, a refusal or an emission flagged as backing no key length, never a default, dropped entry, changed source mode or licence the compiler writes. Passing asserts nothing about the apparatus or attack-set inclusion.
protocol-compiler/thm:gates.title: The emission gates and their outcomes

protocol-compiler/thm:measurements-and-s.summary: Declared measurement families are exact POVMs block by block, per factor and, in POVM form, per Alice sector in the general format; the product and denoted ensemble families are POVMs by theorem. So D(iii) holds, and the statistics are a distribution on every normalised positive block-list state.
protocol-compiler/thm:measurements-and-s.title: Exact measurement families and the statistics functional

protocol-compiler/thm:sifting-and-key.summary: Each announcement is a function of its sender's readout and of the announcements before it, sifting is determined by the announcements, and the holder computes the raw key locally. An ensemble-form measurement slot of Alice's denotes a POVM.
protocol-compiler/thm:sifting-and-key.title: Announcement locality, sifting and party computability

protocol-compiler/thm:typing.summary: A declaration the compilation map emits satisfies the typing conditions D(i), D(ii), D(iv) and D(vi), and its index map is a bijection on every alphabet it indexes. Each follows from the construction or from a check decided on the emitted data, never from a source certificate.
protocol-compiler/thm:typing.title: Typing of an emitted declaration

protocol-compiler/thm:validator-soundnes.summary: Passing the validator's eight checks establishes every target condition of a well-formed declaration, and every check but the feasibility check is complete, so a well-formed declaration is refused only when no default or supplied candidate is verified feasible. Every decision is finite and exact.
protocol-compiler/thm:validator-soundnes.title: Soundness, completeness and decidability of the validator

receiver/ass:eig.summary: Where an exact window is evaluated in floating point, the declared slack bounds any overestimate of the exact block minimum eigenvalue by the computed one. This one-sided premise on the arithmetic is the price of that window; a setting without one, or evaluated rigorously, does not invoke it.
receiver/ass:eig.title: Declared slack on the computed block eigenvalues
receiver/ass:eig.user_statement: Applies only if you request an exact-window depth at a setting whose weight the receiver evaluates in floating point. Wherever your declaration describes a valid receiver exactly, the receiver evaluates the weight rigorously instead, from a proved lower bound on each block eigenvalue, and does not use this premise; the record says which evaluation each setting got. Where it falls back to floating point, the eigensolver that computes the smallest eigenvalue of each requested high-photon block may overestimate it by at most the slack ε_eig you declared. The engine cannot check this and trusts its floating-point eigensolver up to ε_eig. Without an exact-window request this premise is not used, and the bound comes from a closed form that rests on no premise about the eigensolver.

receiver/ass:exact.summary: Declared component parameters, efficiencies, dark-count probabilities and probe mean photon numbers are exact. A non-zero parameter tolerance would be an uncertainty set, which is out of scope and is refused rather than ignored.
receiver/ass:exact.title: Exact declared parameters
receiver/ass:exact.user_statement: Every number you declared for a receiver component (each efficiency, dark-count probability, probe mean photon number and other component parameter) is the device's true value, not an estimate with an error bar. The engine refuses a non-zero tolerance field, and an uncertainty set is not modelled. A result computed from a measured value therefore applies to a device with exactly that value.

receiver/ass:modes.summary: Every optical path from outside the receiver to a detector is a declared mode. A bright-illumination or wavelength-shifted attack targets exactly this premise.
receiver/ass:modes.title: Completeness of the declared modes
receiver/ass:modes.user_statement: Every way light from outside can reach one of your detectors (every spatial, spectral, temporal and polarisation mode it can arrive in) is represented by one of the declared modes. Light the model does not carry, for example at another wavelength or along a path straight to the detectors as in bright-illumination attacks, violates this. Declare the mode, or declare a model of the attack. This premise is about the completeness of the receiver's optical description; that nothing reaches the station except through its declared inputs, and that nothing leaks out of it, is the laboratory premise of this station's party, [[A-LAB]].

receiver/ass:nosel.summary: The receiver configuration and the probe declaration are fixed before the run and cannot be chosen or influenced by the adversary. With [[A-TRUST]] this makes one declared POVM, rather than a family, the right object.
receiver/ass:nosel.title: Device fixed independently of the adversary
receiver/ass:nosel.user_statement: Your receiver's configuration (its components and their settings, which output goes to which detector, and the probe settings) is fixed before the run. An attacker cannot choose or change it, including through properties the model does not describe, such as the wavelength of injected light shifting a beam splitter's ratio. If an attacker can steer the receiver this way, the declared measurement is the wrong one and the result does not apply. This premise is about the configuration of the receiver itself; what may leave or enter the station by other routes is the laboratory premise of this station's party, [[A-LAB]].

receiver/ass:passive.summary: Every optical element is passive linear optics, with no gain and no mixing of creation and annihilation operators. Total photon number is then a conserved grading, on which every block statement of the module rests.
receiver/ass:passive.title: Passive linear optics
receiver/ass:passive.user_statement: Every optical component of your receiver is passive and linear: beam splitters, wave plates, polarisers, attenuators and the like. No component amplifies light, and none is nonlinear (no frequency conversion, no squeezing). The total photon number is then never increased inside the receiver. If a component can add photons, the photon-number blocks the analysis rests on do not exist.

receiver/ass:port.summary: A port clicks exactly when the modes it collects carry at least one photon, whatever their distribution over those modes. It is the multimode form of [[A-THRESH]], and it gives a detector that collects several modes a meaning.
receiver/ass:port.title: Mode-insensitive port response
receiver/ass:port.user_statement: Each detector port clicks exactly when at least one photon arrives in any of the modes it collects, whatever their distribution over those modes. A detector whose click probability depends on the spatial, spectral or temporal mode of the arriving photon (efficiency mismatch) violates this. Such a mismatch has to be declared as mode-dependent loss in front of the port.

receiver/ass:round.summary: The same instrument, probe declaration and dark-count channel describe every round, and the receiver has no memory across rounds. One receiver artifact then describes the whole run.
receiver/ass:round.title: Round homogeneity of the instrument, probe and dark counts
receiver/ass:round.user_statement: Your receiver behaves the same way in every round: the same optics, the same probe settings and the same dark-count behaviour. Nothing it does in one round depends on the inputs or outputs of other rounds: no detector memory, and no drift that the declaration averages over. A receiver whose efficiency drifts during the run violates this. Only parts of a run fixed before it starts, each processed as its own execution and composed under [[A-SEPARATE]], can be analysed separately; a split chosen after seeing the data is not covered. A receiver whose detectors remember earlier clicks, through afterpulsing, a dead time or any other dependence on earlier rounds, violates it too, and nothing in this engine repairs that: no input describes more than one round.

receiver/ass:thresh.summary: Each detector reports one bit per gate, with no photon-number resolution, no memory or timing effects, and no correlations beyond the declared dark-count channel. It fixes the click-or-no-click outcome alphabet the receiver's measurement is built on.
receiver/ass:thresh.title: Threshold detectors without memory
receiver/ass:thresh.user_statement: Your detectors are threshold (click or no-click) detectors read once per gate. They have no photon-number resolution, no dead time, no afterpulsing and no timing jitter. Gates and detectors are correlated only through the dark-count model you declared. Dark counts are independent from round to round, and between detectors unless you declared a correlated dark-count channel. Detectors with dead time or afterpulsing at your gate rate violate this.

receiver/ass:trust.summary: The declared instrument describes the physical receiver exactly, and the receiver is under the legitimate party's control. It is the parent of most of the receiver's device assumptions, which spell out its parts.
receiver/ass:trust.title: Trusted and exactly characterised receiver
receiver/ass:trust.user_statement: The receiver you declared is the receiver you run. Its mode space, its optical layout (or the instrument or Gram matrices you supplied), the assignment of outputs to detectors, the efficiencies, the dark-count probabilities and the probe states are those of the physical device, with no uncertainty to account for. The device is under your control, and nobody else can select, tune or influence it. A characterisation uncertainty is not modelled: the result applies to the device exactly as declared.

receiver/ass:vac.summary: Undeclared input modes and dilation modes start in vacuum. A mode that can carry light to a detector is declared, as a channel mode if the adversary can populate it and as a source mode if the legitimate party does.
receiver/ass:vac.title: Vacuum on undeclared input modes
receiver/ass:vac.user_statement: Every optical input of your receiver that you did not declare as an input, and every internal loss or ancilla mode, receives no light. A mode that can carry light to a detector is declared: as a channel mode if an attacker could put light into it, and as a source mode if your own equipment, for example a probe laser, does.

receiver/cor:emitted-unconditioned.summary: For a receiver without probe modes the one emitted weight bounds the multiclick element on every block above the cutoff and lies in [0, 1], under [[A-EIG]] only where a computed block eigenvalue enters it. The slot entry of the multiclick set meets the guarantee of [[receiver/def:slot]].
receiver/cor:emitted-unconditioned.title: Emitted multiclick weight of a probe-free receiver

receiver/def:compile.summary: The compiled instrument matrix is the product of the embedded elements along a linear extension, later elements multiplying from the left, followed by the terminal detector-efficiency layer. This fixes the matrix convention of the whole receiver contract.
receiver/def:compile.title: Compilation of a declared element graph

receiver/def:graph.summary: A declared element graph is well formed when every element's parameters lie in their domain, the graph is acyclic, and any two elements sharing a mode are ordered by it. Support comparability keeps an arbitrary sort from supplying a physical ordering the declaration left open.
receiver/def:graph.title: Declared element graph

receiver/def:probe.summary: A probe declaration is a finite alphabet of probe settings, vacuum among them, with a declared probe state per setting that is diagonal in the occupation basis. In the Gaussian tier each state is a product of thermal states given by their mean photon numbers.
receiver/def:probe.title: Probe declaration

receiver/def:slot.summary: The artifact carries high-photon lower bounds on disjoint sets of raw outcomes, one weight per set and setting; a set's uniform weight is its minimum over the settings. The receiver carries one entry, the multiclick set with the per-setting multiclick weights.
receiver/def:slot.title: The strengthening slot

receiver/detector-imperfections/prop:eff.summary: Every click pattern of a probe-free receiver is the pull-back, through the pure-loss channel of the factored loss t, of the same pattern of its normalized station, and so is every dark-count composition. The statistics agree, and the loss can be handed to the adversary.
receiver/detector-imperfections/prop:eff.title: A receiver as uniform loss followed by its normalized station
receiver/detector-imperfections/prop:eff.user_statement: If your receiver has no probe source, the largest of its detector efficiencies can be treated as uniform loss in front of the whole receiver, followed by a receiver whose best detector is perfect and whose other detectors keep their efficiencies relative to it. The dark counts stay at the detectors. Both descriptions give the same click probabilities for every input, so the loss in front can be counted as part of the channel the adversary controls. A detector efficiency that depends on time slot, wavelength or spatial mode is covered if declared as mode-dependent loss in front of the detector, which stays in place; a dependence on a degree of freedom the adversary can use but your declaration does not carry is efficiency mismatch, which this does not address.

receiver/req:graph-refusal.summary: A declared element graph failing any of (E1) to (E3) is refused with the failing condition named, and the offending element or edge for (E1) or element pair for (E3). No matrix is emitted and no ordering is invented.
receiver/req:graph-refusal.title: Refusal of a graph that is not well formed

receiver/req:probe-diagonal-admission.summary: The engine admits declared probe states of the Gaussian tier only, which are occupation-diagonal by construction, and refuses any other. Conditioning on an admitted probe therefore keeps the channel photon-number blocks.
receiver/req:probe-diagonal-admission.title: Admission of Gaussian-tier probe states only

receiver/thm:emitted-bound.summary: Each setting's emitted weight bounds its multiclick element on every photon-number block above the cutoff, and their minimum does so at every setting, under the eigenvalue-slack assumption [[A-EIG]] only where computed block eigenvalues enter. Each weight lies in [0, 1] and is finitely computable.
receiver/thm:emitted-bound.title: Multiclick bounds carried by the emitted weights

reductions/ass:constdecl.summary: Every constant of an emitted constraint entry is fixed before the run by the device fact that certifies it and is no function of an observed statistic. Observed data reach the analysis only through the acceptance set, which belongs to another module.
reductions/ass:constdecl.title: Declared constants of the constraint list
reductions/ass:constdecl.user_statement: Applies only where the reduction emits constraints on the attacker; a run that emits none does not rest on it. Every number used as a constant in such a constraint (for example a bound on a detector's multi-photon response) is fixed before the run from the device characterisation that justifies it. It is never adjusted using data observed in the run; observed data enter only through the acceptance test.

reductions/ass:meas.summary: In every round each measuring party's device acts as one POVM: it emits a classical outcome, retains no quantum system, and everything after it acts on classical data. It is the hypothesis about the devices behind the output-state equality of the physical and the squashed protocol.
reductions/ass:meas.title: Each measuring party's device as one POVM per round
reductions/ass:meas.user_statement: Each measuring device, at every measuring station of either party, turns the incoming quantum signal into a classical result in every round and keeps nothing quantum afterwards: no post-measurement system is stored, re-used or passed on. Everything after detection (announcements, sifting, acceptance, the key map, error correction, privacy amplification) uses classical data only. Where several measuring stations are declared, of different parties or of one, or where several parties measure inside one declared station, each device measures independently of the others, so that the round's measurement is the product of theirs: no shared randomness or shared ancilla couples them. A receiver with a quantum memory that keeps the measured light, or passes it on, violates this.

reductions/ass:probe.summary: A station's private per-round setting is drawn from its party's own randomness with the declared class weights, independently of the adversary and the round's quantum input, never inferred from an outcome. It lets the setting enter a joint outcome under one common squashing channel.
reductions/ass:probe.title: The station's private setting drawn from its own declared randomness
reductions/ass:probe.user_statement: The station's private setting in each round (for the optical instance, how its probe is switched) is chosen by a random number generator of the station's own party with exactly the declared probabilities. It is independent of anything the attacker does and of the light arriving in that round, and it is never derived from a detection result. An attacker who can predict or influence the setting violates this.

reductions/ass:recv.summary: A supplier artefact read by a reduction instance is that module's own output at the accepted version it declares, and the device facts its claims state hold of the numbers exactly as declared. It is the premise behind a reduction on supplier numbers, save an exact, rigorous artefact the run built.
reductions/ass:recv.title: Supplier artefact whose claims hold of the device
reductions/ass:recv.user_statement: The receiver data your reduction uses (blocks, high-photon weights with their quantifier domain, dark-count channel) come from a receiver artefact produced by an accepted version of the receiver module, the version the artefact names, on the inputs it names, with its own validation results attached, and the device facts that module's claims state are true of those numbers exactly as declared, under its own assumptions. Where this run built it from a declaration describing a valid receiver exactly, every weight evaluated rigorously, both halves follow and the report omits this premise ([[reductions/req:recv-row-provenance]]). For another artefact this run built, acceptance is the status the report gives the receiver's claims and you rely on the second half, floating-point weights included; a receiver file from outside the run needs your own justification for both halves.

reductions/ass:round.summary: One physical POVM describes the measurement of every round, and each round's measurement acts as it describes whatever happened in other rounds: no detector memory and no drift. Nothing is assumed about the attacks being independent across rounds.
reductions/ass:round.title: Round homogeneity of the physical measurement
reductions/ass:round.user_statement: Each measuring device, at every measuring station of either party, performs the same measurement in every round: the same optics, detectors and dark-count behaviour, settings drawn with the same probabilities, and, where you declared detector-response modes, the same response in each mode. What a device does in one round does not depend on the inputs or outputs of other rounds. Drift of efficiency, alignment or dark counts violates this. Only parts of a run fixed before it starts, each processed as its own execution and composed under [[A-SEPARATE]], can be analysed separately; a split chosen after seeing the data is not covered. Detector memory (afterpulsing, a dead time, any dependence on earlier rounds) violates it too, and nothing here repairs that. Attacks may still correlate the rounds. The engine's finite model and squashing map are its own construction, not part of this premise.

reductions/ass:tsm.summary: Every per-round public choice of known bias at the measurement the emitted family describes, its private setting included where it has one, is a component of the emitted outcome and enters only through its statistics. No derivation then assumes a state-independent test fraction.
reductions/ass:tsm.title: Output-state test statistics
reductions/ass:tsm.user_statement: Every per-round random choice with a known bias made at this station (for example its probe setting, where it has one, or whether a round is a test round, where that is added by relabelling its outcomes) is recorded as part of that round's outcome, and it enters the analysis only through the observed statistics. No derivation of this contract then assumes a state-independent test fraction.

reductions/cor:reference-companion.summary: The same instance, run on the reference in place of the snap, or on its own snapped blocks where none is handed, is a reduction instance of the emitted shape that squashes that model exactly. Its entries are enclosed from the reference, requested ones where their certificates hold there.
reductions/cor:reference-companion.title: The reference companion of a reduction instance

reductions/def:protocol.summary: An n-round protocol passes each round's measured system, held by the measuring parties, through one measurement channel, the same in every round, and no later processing touches that system. The squashed protocol is the same channel with the target POVM in place of the physical one.
reductions/def:protocol.title: Measurement-factorizing n-round protocol

reductions/req:recv-row-provenance.summary: The ledger omits [[A-RECV]] only where every supplier artefact read is a receiver artefact this run built, with a model admissible exactly and every weight evaluated rigorously. Both clauses then hold by the receiver's theorems under its own ledger, with no premise on arithmetic.
reductions/req:recv-row-provenance.title: Omission of the supplier row for a receiver artefact the run built
reductions/req:recv-row-provenance.user_statement: Where this run built the receiver artefact itself from your declared receiver, your declaration describes a valid receiver exactly, and every high-photon weight was computed rigorously, the report does not list the premise that a supplied receiver file is genuine and true of your device ([[A-RECV]]). What that premise says then follows from the receiver's theorems under the receiver's own assumptions, which the report lists, and whether those theorems are accepted is shown by their status in the report. Wherever a weight was evaluated in floating point, the receiver was admitted only within its tolerances, or the receiver file came from outside the run, the report keeps [[A-RECV]].

reductions/thm:emit.summary: The emitted target is computed exactly, decided exactly admissible before emission, and squashes the declared model exactly; nearness to the handed model bounds nothing. On blocks the record names as resting on [[A-SNAP]], the run's conclusions about the device rest on that premise.
reductions/thm:emit.title: Exact emission of a reduction instance

reductions/thm:licence.summary: If each operator the squashing carries pulls back to a physical operator ≤, = or ≥ a multiple of the identity, every squashed physical attack respects the resulting constraint list in either source mode, factor by factor for per-factor bounds. Security against such attacks transfers with the same ε.
reductions/thm:licence.title: The attack-set licence

reductions/wpfss/cor:emitted-flat.summary: The flat instance's emitted family is exactly admissible and pulls back exactly to the declared model on the channel system, its weights rounded down yet certified. Where the normalizer moved a block below the cutoff, nearness to the unrounded family bounds nothing.
reductions/wpfss/cor:emitted-flat.title: Exact emission of the flat instance

reductions/wpfss/cor:flat-companion.summary: Run on any Hermitian, positive receiver blocks complete per setting, the flat instance forms, as a non-negative combination of them, an admissible datum over the reals, as the core companion asks. A requested two-sector entry keeps its certificate where the centres clear its constant by the radius.
reductions/wpfss/cor:flat-companion.title: The flat instance has a reference companion

statistics/ass:alphabet.summary: In every one of the n rounds of the run an acceptance value of the alphabet is recorded. The counts and the frequency vector then describe the whole run, normalised by its round count.
statistics/ass:alphabet.title: An acceptance value recorded in every round
statistics/ass:alphabet.user_statement: Every one of the n rounds of your run records an acceptance value from the declared acceptance alphabet: no round counted in n is missing from the record. If rounds go missing (for example through lost time tags), the counts are normalised against the wrong number of rounds and the acceptance test does not describe the run. A round missing from the record also puts security at stake: the acceptance test must be evaluated on the acceptance values of all n rounds ([[A-CONFORM]]), and a measured round the record drops is a sifting step the declaration does not describe ([[A-SPEC]]). Where the engine builds the acceptance set, it checks that the alphabet, its order and n are those of your protocol declaration; a set carried in the declaration is read in the declaration's order, so writing it in that order is yours to check.

statistics/ass:hon.summary: On an honest run the acceptance statistics are independent and identically distributed with the declared law. The premise bears on the advertised honest abort probability and restricts no adversary.
statistics/ass:hon.title: Honest i.i.d. rounds
statistics/ass:hon.user_statement: Without an eavesdropper, every round's acceptance outcome is drawn independently from the same declared distribution. If you expect drift between or within runs, declare an honest envelope instead. This premise only bears on the advertised probability that an honest run aborts: if it fails, an honest run may abort more or less often than advertised. Security is unaffected.

statistics/ass:hon-env.summary: On an honest run each round's probability of each acceptance outcome, given everything before it, stays inside the declared honest envelope. The premise bears on the advertised honest abort probability and restricts no adversary.
statistics/ass:hon-env.title: Honest rounds inside a declared envelope
statistics/ass:hon-env.user_statement: When no attacker is present, each round's probability of each acceptance outcome, given everything that happened before, stays inside the honest model: between the lower and upper bounds of the honest envelope where you declared one, and equal to the honest distribution where you gave a single one instead (an envelope of zero width). With an envelope the channel may drift within and between runs as long as it stays inside it; with a single distribution it may not drift at all. This premise only bears on the advertised probability that an honest run aborts; it never affects security. If drift can leave the honest model, declare a wider envelope.

statistics/ass:reach.summary: Some feasible state of the consuming declaration produces a law of the declared honest envelope, for a single declared law that law itself. It rules out an incompatibility of the honest model with the declaration.
statistics/ass:reach.title: An honest law produced by a feasible state
statistics/ass:reach.user_statement: Your honest model fits your protocol declaration: a state the declaration admits as feasible produces acceptance statistics in your declared honest envelope, or equal to your single declared honest law. If it fails, the declared devices do not describe the statistics and a key length for them is not warranted. The engine's own honest models are built to match the declared Alice marginal; nothing proves this premise for them. Unless switched off, the engine checks every run whose honest statistics you supply or whose declaration carries a constraint you declared: from a proven mismatch it states a cap on the probability that devices behaving as the declaration says pass your acceptance test, and refuses the run where that cap is at most one half, a threshold you can set. On an unchecked run a mismatch goes undetected and this premise is yours to vouch for.

statistics/binomial-box/def:construction.summary: The construction map bounds each constrained outcome by its guarded count endpoints divided by the round count, gives every other outcome the bounds 0 and 1, and intersects the box with the probability simplex. Its output is a polytope in canonical box form built from the honest envelope.
statistics/binomial-box/def:construction.title: The construction map

statistics/binomial-box/req:completeness.summary: The engine reports ε* itself on the exact rule evaluated by its closed forms, and otherwise the figure its route's row names: the allocation sum or an upward-rounded evaluation of the tails clamped at the budget. It never reports a downward-rounded figure.
statistics/binomial-box/req:completeness.title: The reported completeness figure

statistics/binomial-box/req:input-refusa.summary: Before constructing anything the engine decides every condition of an admissible input its inputs determine; on a violation it reports the first by its code and emits no acceptance set, repairing nothing. Data not of the input's form, with the request defaults in place, are refused too.
statistics/binomial-box/req:input-refusa.title: Refusal of an input that violates a decidable clause

statistics/binomial-box/thm:completeness.summary: If each honest round's conditional outcome law stays inside the envelope, an honest run fails the acceptance test with probability at most ε*, the sum of the binomial tails at the envelope's ends beyond the box's count bounds, and ε* is at most the completeness budget. No independence is needed.
statistics/binomial-box/thm:completeness.title: The completeness bound

statistics/binomial-box/thm:honest-conta.summary: Every law of the envelope set lies in the constructed box for every budget and allocation, so a reachable one gives a compatible pair and rules out the consuming engine's infeasibility condition. The construction never fails on an admissible input, so every refusal comes from the input.
statistics/binomial-box/thm:honest-conta.title: Honest containment and infeasibility

statistics/req:matched-alphabet.summary: An acceptance set is docked only on the alphabet, in its declared enumeration, and the round count of the declaration its consumer solves: a built set is compared with the declaration first, a set the declaration carries is read in that enumeration. A disagreement produces no result.
statistics/req:matched-alphabet.title: Alphabet and round count taken from the consuming declaration

statistics/singleton/thm:singleton-compl.summary: Under i.i.d. honest rounds a singleton acceptance set accepts with its point's multinomial probability. That is 0, with no completeness budget below one, if n times a coordinate is no integer or the point leaves the law's support; else the least budget is one minus it, zero only for one point mass.
statistics/singleton/thm:singleton-compl.title: Completeness of a singleton acceptance set

statistics/thm:box-oracle.summary: Over a non-empty canonical box, filling the coordinates of smallest coefficient first minimises a rational linear functional exactly, with a dual witness of the same value. The outcomes with a positive upper bound include every outcome on which a point of the box puts weight, and can include more.
statistics/thm:box-oracle.title: Acceptance support and the exact box oracle

transmitter/ass:ens.summary: The physical source draws each round's letter independently with the declared weights and emits the product of the declared states, no round depending on another. It ties a source specification declared as matrices to the device it describes.
transmitter/ass:ens.title: Emission of the specified ensemble
transmitter/ass:ens.user_statement: Your source prepares, in every round, one of the declared states with the declared probabilities. Each round's letter is drawn independently with weights p_x, and the states emitted over the n rounds form a product: no round's letter or state depends on another round, its detection results or its public messages. A source with memory or drift between rounds (for example pattern effects in a modulator) violates this. Where your source is a pair source inside your laboratory with one half measured there to herald or fix the letter, those local detectors belong to the declared ensemble: their efficiency mismatch must be carried by the declared weights and states, and their memory across rounds (for example afterpulsing or dead time) violates this like any other dependence between rounds.

transmitter/ass:seq.summary: Each round runs the delivery of its quantum systems, then every party's measurement, then the round's public messages, then sifting; each party measures in round order, post-processing follows all rounds and every message is public. It is the timing premise of the security analysis.
transmitter/ass:seq.title: Sequential round structure
transmitter/ass:seq.user_statement: In every round the quantum systems come first: where your source is trusted, it prepares and sends that round's signal, and otherwise the systems of the round are delivered to the measuring stations. Then every party that measures completes its measurement, and only then are that round's public messages sent, in the declared order. Sifting is then determined by the announcements, and no operation on a quantum system of a round depends on a public message of that round. All classical post-processing (for example error correction, verification and privacy amplification) runs after all n rounds, and every classical message is public. A message sent before a measurement of the same round has finished (for example an early basis announcement) violates this. Each party that measures completes its measurement of each round before it completes that of the next round.

transmitter/ass:src.summary: In trusted-source mode the retained system A stays in the laboratory of the party that holds it and is acted on only by that party's declared measurement, condition (SR3) of the certificate. It is what lets a declared marginal delete attacks.
transmitter/ass:src.title: Retention of the system A in trusted-source mode
transmitter/ass:src.user_statement: The source's retained half, system A, never leaves the laboratory of the party the declaration assigns it to, and nothing acts on it except that party's own declared measurement: no other step of the protocol and no action of the adversary. In a prepare-and-measure setup A exists only in the source-replacement description, and this is the premise that the adversary has no access to that party's laboratory. Only then may you declare the source's reduced state τ_A (trusted-source mode), which removes attacks from the analysis when A has dimension at least two. If you cannot vouch for this, use untrusted-source mode: the key rate can only drop, and the result stays valid.

transmitter/decoy/ass:wcp.summary: The physical source emits exactly the declared phase-randomised weak coherent state of each round's letter, drawn with its declared weight, in the declared modes only and independently across rounds. It ties the tagged declaration to the device, in the place of [[A-ENS]].
transmitter/decoy/ass:wcp.title: Emission of the declared weak-coherent-pulse states
transmitter/decoy/ass:wcp.user_statement: Your weak-coherent-pulse source emits, in every round, a fully phase-randomised coherent pulse at exactly the declared intensity μ and polarisation, in the two declared optical modes only, and nothing else; the numbers are those of your tagged declaration, exactly as declared. No other property of the pulse (timing, spectrum, spatial shape) depends on the chosen bit, basis, intensity or round type, and the round type (test or generation) changes nothing emitted. Intensities do not fluctuate. Each round's letter is drawn independently with the declared probabilities, and no round's letter or emitted pulse depends on another round, its detection results or its public messages. Intensity fluctuations, imperfect phase randomisation or pattern effects violate this.

transmitter/decoy/cor:emitted-decoy.summary: The emitted decoy declaration has an exact certificate against the tagged ensemble, its source identity by the tagging channel, and block-diagonal attacked states. Exactness is decided on products of declared weights and formed dyad entries; lowering a weight gives another tagged declaration.
transmitter/decoy/cor:emitted-decoy.title: The emitted decoy declaration

transmitter/fact:sr.summary: Preparing labelled signals is equivalent to preparing purifications with a shield system and measuring a retained label register. This is the entanglement-based description on which the trusted-source constraints of the module rest.
transmitter/fact:sr.title: Source replacement for prepare-and-measure protocols

transmitter/thm:certificate-sufficiency.summary: In any form (pure projector, sector blocks, ensemble presentation) the certificate's algebraic conditions are finitely many exact decisions making Alice's measurement reproduce the virtual ensemble. Under retention and sequential rounds she may measure before or after any attack: source replacement.
transmitter/thm:certificate-sufficiency.title: Checkability and sufficiency of the source-replacement certificate
